Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

📅 23 Dec 2025 | ⏱️ 2 min read (459 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died.
  • According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles.
  • It has been revealed that vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

It has been revealed that vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

Zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

In a recent development, respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA noted in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that “While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the Aurora roster lists Boo, chiwa, Derke, B1SK and trexx.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aurora Gaming came from a map down to beat F9 EICAR 2-1 and win the first VCT EMEA Kickoff Europe open qualifier. The win came days after they were put back into the bracket when the UK team BONK was disqualified for cheating.

In a recent development, the VCT EMEA Kickoff: Europe Qualifier 2027 decider got under way at 18:45. The series began on Lotus. Aurora’s chiwa was named most valuable player of the series.

In a recent development, the Aurora roster lists Boo, chiwa, Derke, B1SK and trexx. F9 EICAR, based in France, fielded Kipperman, Destrian, Tenshi, izana and Geekkooo.

Aurora’s run nearly ended early. BONK, a UK Valorant roster, beat them 2-1 in the round of 32 on 6 November. That result followed a comeback from 3-11 down on Bind. Riot’s ruling against BONK reversed Aurora’s exit. Every BONK player and registered team member was provisionally suspended. Project 100K and ycatble returned to the bracket along with Aurora.

The qualifier left no room for error. It was a single-elimination bracket for 256 teams, and every match was a best-of-three. Once reinstated, Aurora did not drop a map before the final. They beat Pixel Lumina 2-0 in the second semi-final.

In the first semi-final, xXxMasterProMegaTeamxXx fell 2-1 to F9 EICAR. The French side had arrived at the qualifier in mixed form. F9 EICAR lost 0-2 to WIP Esports in VCL France: Revolution Stage 2 2026 and were twice beaten 1-2 by Mandatory. A 2-1 result against Esprit Shōnen was their only victory in that run.

Recent findings suggest that the Elo power rankings show the gap on paper. F9 EICAR sit at rank 241, with a rating of 1405 and a 6-16 record in 22 rated matches. Aurora are unranked.

The final still carried weight. Seeding for the playoff stage would be decided by the result, Insider Gaming reported.

In a recent development, the stakes are clear. Under Riot’s 2027 system, four non-partner teams will reach VCT EMEA Kickoff. Two will come from Europe, one from Türkiye and one from the Middle East and North Africa.

— Aurora Valorant (@Aurora_Valorant) November 10, 2026.

That leaves European hopefuls chasing places at a 12-team LAN event. VCT 2027 EMEA Kickoff will be run by Riot Games at the Riot Games Arena in Berlin.

The playoff field is not yet complete. The top four teams from each open qualifier move on, and the second Europe open qualifier is set for 12 to 15 November. The playoffs will use a modified double-elimination bracket of best-of-three matches, with a best-of-five grand final. The top two finishers earn places at VCT 2027 EMEA Kickoff, whose window runs from 14 January to 7 February.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros patch brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

For one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The upgrade is also adding some notable new features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

Throne of Eros also doubles as the upcoming Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

Sources indicate that there’s also the Memory Growth Bonus, another limited-time event that you can take advantage of to grow your Memories. The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock newly introduced second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

On the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two fresh main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

Recent findings suggest that the celebrations also extend to newly introduced anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Beyond the anniversary content, version 5.0 also adds a new feature to the game: Home, which essentially offers a hub to get you directly to interacting with love interests that doesn’t have to do with combat or story.

You can also expect various other quality of life updates that touch on the Journal, Phone Moments Search, Resources Quick Cleanup, and latest Tete-a-Tete that should make interacting with all of them more streamlined.

While this is a special banner, you should brush up on how banners work in Love and Deepspace if you’re unfamiliar. As always, it’s never not a good idea to check our Love and Deepspace codes page for some freebies.

Vitamin B12 may hold the key to treating a rare genetic disorder

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (692 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A surprising discovery involving vitamin B12 could open new possibilities for understanding and potentially treating rare genetic disorders.
  • The findings center on a cellular process called RNA splicing, which helps prepare the genetic instructions cells use to produce proteins.
  • According to recent reports, mutations in genes responsible for splicing can cause conditions such as Verheij syndrome.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A surprising discovery involving vitamin B12 could open new possibilities for understanding and potentially treating rare genetic disorders. Researchers found that the vitamin can correct developmental problems in tiny worms carrying a genetic mutation associated with Verheij syndrome, a rare human condition that causes developmental delays, impaired growth, and short stature.

The findings center on a cellular process called RNA splicing, which helps prepare the genetic instructions cells use to produce proteins. During splicing, unnecessary portions of messenger RNA are removed, and the remaining sections are joined together in the correct order. When this process goes wrong, it can disrupt essential cellular functions and contribute to serious developmental disorders.

According to recent reports, mutations in genes responsible for splicing can cause conditions such as Verheij syndrome. To better understand the effects of these genetic changes, scientists investigated how a related mutation affects growth and metabolism in a laboratory model.

Vitamin B12 Reverses Developmental Defects in Worms.

It has been revealed that the discovery emerged from experiments involving C. elegans, a tiny roundworm commonly used in biological research. The researchers were initially searching for previously unknown genes that influence lifespan when they began examining a mutation in a gene involved in RNA splicing. The same gene is associated with Verheij syndrome in humans.

Industry observers note that worms carrying the mutation developed problems resembling important features of the human disorder. Their growth slowed considerably, and they remained smaller than normal.

Recent findings suggest that to investigate why this happened, the scientists conducted genetic screens and analyzed the worms' metabolism. They discovered that the mutation disrupted specific metabolic pathways that depend on vitamin B12 and are essential for healthy growth and normal cellular activity.

Sources indicate that the researchers then tested whether providing additional vitamin B12 could counteract these changes. Remarkably, the treatment restored the affected metabolic processes to normal and corrected the developmental abnormalities associated with the mutation.

"We were surprised to find that a change in a fundamental process of RNA processing had such a targeted effect on vitamin B12-dependent metabolism," says Jonathan Kölschbach, first author of the study. "Even more exciting was that we were able to largely correct the consequences of this change in the worm model using vitamin B12.".

Could Vitamin B12 Help Treat a Rare Genetic Disorder?

Recent findings suggest that to explore whether their findings might also apply to people, the researchers examined publicly available datasets from human cells. They also worked with Hormos Dafsari, a neuropediatrician at the University Hospital Cologne, to collect blood samples from patients diagnosed with Verheij syndrome.

These investigations uncovered evidence of similar metabolic changes in humans, suggesting that the vitamin B12-related pathways affected in the worms may also play a role in the human disorder.

Although the results are promising, researchers have not yet established whether vitamin B12 supplementation can improve symptoms in people with Verheij syndrome. Additional studies will be necessary to determine whether the benefits observed in worms can be translated into a treatment for patients.

Recent findings suggest that the discovery also raises a broader possibility. Metabolic disruptions may contribute more substantially to diseases caused by faulty RNA splicing than scientists previously recognized. Understanding these connections could help researchers identify new therapeutic strategies, potentially extending beyond Verheij syndrome to other rare genetic conditions.

Industry observers note that "Our study is a good example of how basic research on model organisms can provide newly introduced insights into human diseases," says Adam Antebi, Director at the Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing and lead author of the study. "A fundamental biological question can thus give rise to a new approach that could also become medically relevant in the long term.".

Say what you like about Brawlhalla, but Ubisoft's Smash-like fighting game has chugged along quite nicely whereas other crossover-focused fighters like Multiversus have flagged. Now, Brawlhalla is reaching outside their usual crop of guest fighters to bring in the cast of none other than My Hero Academia!

Sources indicate that set to launch December 9th, the Brawhalla x My Hero Academia crossover features the hotblooded Katsuki Bakugo, coldblooded Shoto Todoroki and, of course, Izuki Midoriya aka Deku himself as brand-new brawlers. Recent findings suggest that as for Brawlhalla, I wasn't kidding when I gave it praise for outlasting Multiversus. And I think part of that is the fact their increasing number of crossover fighters actually have some relevance to the world of gaming and brawling in general. That, and the fact they already had a solid core roster of original fighters means that the novelty of crossover characters remains just that; novel.

In contrast, when Midoriya, Todoroki and Bakugo arrive in My Hero Academia come December 9th, they'll be bringing exciting abilities and fighting styles that'll fit right in with the rest of the Brawlhalla cast already!

Genshin Impact Version Luna 4 introduces three latest playable characters, including the long-awaited Moon Maiden Columbina

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4.
  • Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three latest playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.
  • Recent findings suggest that the first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three latest playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

Recent findings suggest that the first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

It has been revealed that the Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Sources indicate that speaking of elemental reactions, fresh in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Industry observers note that luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the newly introduced Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

In a recent development, the first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a fresh outfit in the shop at a discount.

In a recent development, version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside upcoming stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

#17241. 10 Best Strategy Games Still Stuck on Older Systems

10 Best Strategy Games Still Stuck on Older Systems

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1571 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that in the world of strategy games, it can be really difficult to find one that you like that really fits what you’re looking for.
  • Recent findings suggest that it’s always a bit of a tossup for most any game that’s released on older consoles, except Skyrim and GTA V which seemingly never stop being rereleased.
  • Recent findings suggest that this list is a collection of some of the best strategy games that got left behind over the years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in the world of strategy games, it can be really difficult to find one that you like that really fits what you’re looking for. Unfortunately, even when you do find a great strategy game, there’s always the chance that it won’t ever be upgraded or receive a good sequel.

Recent findings suggest that it’s always a bit of a tossup for most any game that’s released on older consoles, except Skyrim and GTA V which seemingly never stop being rereleased. Some games aren’t as fortunate, despite how good they might be.

Recent findings suggest that this list is a collection of some of the best strategy games that got left behind over the years. Whether it’s turn-based or real time strategy, each and every one of these games fits the bill and most definitely deserves to be brought back from the dead.

Recent findings suggest that many games based around mechs end up running into issues concerning the depth and skill required to play. Thankfully for Front Mission 4, the developers managed to figure out how to raise the game to a upcoming level.

Front Mission 4 is actually a prequel game set before the events of Front Mission 2, bringing to life the story of two characters from the past. Players take control of the mechs piloted by our protagonists as they attempt to uncover what happened during an attack on some military bases.

In a recent development, the turn-based nature of the game combined with some interesting and fun mechanics makes Front Mission 4 a great candidate for a remake. The game was received generally favorably, although it was a bit sluggish in the narrative department.

In a recent development, would any list of classic games be complete without the obligatory obscure JRPG? We certainly don’t think so, which is why Stella Deus: The Gate of Eternity is here. This strange JRPG feels almost like a precursor to Triangle Strategy with how it's set up.

According to recent reports, while similar to other JRPGs in the sense of controlling a party with various classes and abilities, the game also dove heavily into the political side of things. Playing as Spero, players must navigate the difficult political challenges while trying to stop the Miasma from destroying the world.

It has been revealed that the game had interesting stakes along with a solid story exploring some harsher topics than most. This let it land fairly well amongst critics, though the lacking AI and outstanding difficulty of the game drew some ire.

Back in ye olden days of gaming, there was a glorious time where the PlayStation Portable had some truly incredible games. One of these was the tactical war game, Field Commander, which made some definitive waves when it was released.

Much like many war games, players could choose a faction and a commander which had an impact on the army’s skills and weaknesses. This led to some more than interesting choices between the factions and how each one played.

In a recent development, clearly some people really enjoyed it, as it won IGN’s award for Best PSP Strategy Game of 2006. It had some excellent ideas, and might still fare well in today's landscape given the chance.

As the fourth entry into the Rebelstar series, created by Julian Gollop the creator of X-COM, it sought to upgrade the previous games in the series while making the experience more accessible to many people. With some hardcore tactical gameplay and great game design, it landed fairly well.

Industry observers note that A truly old school plot about aliens taking over the world and a resistance rising up to fight them off ensued, and we made some truly disturbing discoveries along the way. Picking up enemy weapons and using everything the battlefield gives you were key parts of this turn-based game.

Praised highly for its combat mechanics, the game was enjoyed, although it did have complications with a lackluster story and lack of support features. Still the game made quite the impact and having that combat in the modern game generation would be nice.

Many games will attempt to make some major changes to their gameplay in an effort to reach a different set of players, and Age of Empires: Mythologies was one such game. It moved from an RTS style game to a purely turn-based one taking after the game before it.

Recent findings suggest that it still worked relatively the same as previous titles, with turn-based choices resulting in battles and collecting resources. The major draw was being able to choose a particular mythology and use units, abilities, and technologies from that mythology to conquer your enemies.

According to recent reports, while Age of Mythologies was remade for the latest generation, this game was sadly left behind. It definitely brings something new to the table, especially for fans of Age of Mythology who may not really enjoy the RTS aspects, and it's a shame it hasn't been revisited.

It may sound similar to Age of Empires II: The Age of Kings, but this game is definitely different and only released for the Nintendo DS. This spin-off title changed up the RTS game and made it into a turn-based title, in an effort to make it easier to play on the handheld device.

In a recent development, playing as one of the five civilizations available, players would get a hero unit along with a more defined set of units based on their civilization. Aside from combat, players could upgrade their civilizations into a new age, giving them access to more units and different technologies.

It shares many qualities with games like Civilization, though the hero aspect makes it a bit unique and would make for a good addition to the turn-based genre in this day and age. It was a solid game with great mechanics, and there was something to be remarked for its smaller number of civilizations and lack of online play.

In a recent development, there are a good number of alternate history war games, but Ring of Red was well ahead of its time. The game sought to combine turn-based and RTS mechanics to create a truly unique gameplay experience.

Recent findings suggest that in a post-WWII world where Japan is split in half, what is effectively a civil war breaks out. Players would set up their units and move them in a turn-based fashion, before switching to a real time combat system.

The mechanics and design of the game made for a unique experience, especially given the mixed gameplay elements. While simple, the game offers some deeper elements, making it a fantastic strategy game by all accounts.

Industry observers note that most everyone at some point played an Advance Wars game if they had a DS. These are some of the best strategy titles on Nintendo handhelds. One of the very best ones was Advance Wars: Days of Ruin, thanks to some well-chosen upgrades to the systems in place.

A much darker and heavier story with some difficult threads and topics to cover, the game was set during a post-apocalyptic war. Players used Commanding Officers with special abilities to turn the tide of battle, while using various units to wipe out the enemy.

Industry observers note that with the new units and mechanics, the game was fairly different from past entries, and praised heavily for that change. Though the story was much darker and many critics found that a bit perturbing due to the past nature of the games, it was a bold change rarely made to Nintendo-published series.

While perhaps not the first god game, Black & White did manage to get critical acclaim thanks to a variety of reasons. The game was made by Fable creator Peter Molyneux, and clearly infuses his unique game design and world building experience into the genre.

Recent findings suggest that players act as a god attempting to lead their people to victory over another rival god, by using their people to perform various acts. The game even has a morality system for players to use, to help them determine how their people feel about them and how they’re doing as a god.

Recent findings suggest that black & White was received incredibly well, and was both nominated for and won several awards. There’s no denying that seeing a game like this for the modern generation would be something amazing. There's something very special about this early effort.

While Advance Wars: Dual Strike may not be the first Advance Wars game in the series, it is arguably the most loved. This interesting take on the turn-based genre really put the Advance Wars series on the map for the mechanics it introduced.

Sources indicate that much like the rest of the series, players could use COs to control the battlefield while they attempted to wipe out the enemy units with their own. The biggest difference was the introduction of a Dual Front system, in which two separate battles occurred on each of the screens of the DS. Touchscreen control also worked very well and practically, without feeling shoehorned in.

By all accounts, the game was a raging succes,s with many calling it a significant improvement over the past titles. Though the game didn’t offer too much beyond the single newly introduced mechanic, it's still praised as one of the greatest turn-based strategy games ever made.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

T1 has added two-time Masters champion Tyson 'TenZ' Ngo to its Valorant roster for VCT Pacific in 2027. The move ends his retirement and builds on T1's signing of crashies, who has just left London-based Fnatic.

Industry observers note that T1 has ended Tyson ‘TenZ’ Ngo’s retirement. The organisation confirmed on 12 November that he will join its Valorant roster for VCT Pacific in 2027. It made the announcement with a post and a welcome video.

T1 called him a ‘living legend’ of Valorant. It mentioned he was starting a upcoming chapter with the organisation.

It has been revealed that tenZ retired from professional play in 2024. He has spent this year at T1 as a content creator. The announcement moves him from that role into the competitive squad.

His record explains the attention. With Sentinels, he beat Fnatic 3-0 in the Masters Reykjavík 2021 final. He then won Masters Madrid 2024 with a 3-2 win over Gen.G. That made him the first Americas player to win more than one VCT Masters event, Liquipedia records.

The TenZ news came a day after T1 confirmed Austin ‘crashies’ Roberts. He returns six years after T1 released him in September 2020. crashies called T1 the place ‘where it all started’. He remarked he was excited for the fresh challenge.

According to recent reports, he played for Fnatic from 11 December 2024 until 4 November 2026. He joined T1 on 11 November 2026.

His exit is part of a wider reshuffle at the London-based organisation. Fnatic lost the Masters Toronto 2025 grand final 3-1 to Paper Rex. It then lost the Valorant Champions 2025 grand final in Paris 3-2 to NRG. On 2 November, Fnatic released head coach Andrey ‘ENGH’ Sholokhov. It stated it was making changes ahead of the 2027 season.

Sources indicate that T1 has also kept some continuity. It extended BuZz’s contract on 6 November 2026. The fresh deal runs until the end of 2028.

Sources indicate that the VCT structure for 2027 was declared on 28 October. Under it, the eight Pacific partner teams go straight into Kickoff in January 2027. The other four Kickoff places go to teams from regional open qualifiers.

It has been revealed that the KING is back! 👑A living legend of VALORANT, 'TenZ' begins a new chapter with T1.Ready to make history under the red wings, join us in giving him a warm welcome!

📺 https://t.co/ny3VtTtYnx#T1VALORANT pic.twitter.com/gmgLEzXJR2.

— T1 VALORANT (@T1) November 12, 2026.

Before Kickoff, T1 has a date in Los Angeles. It is one of six teams directly invited to Red Bull Home Ground 2026. Fnatic, Sentinels, G2 Esports, NRG and ZETA DIVISION have also been invited. That puts the former clubs of both TenZ and crashies in the same field as T1.

The event runs from 10 to 13 December. Group stage matches are on 10 and 11 December. Bracket play and the semi-finals follow on 12 December. The grand final is on 13 December.

Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (987 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that as quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them?
  • It has been revealed that the technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results.
  • According to recent reports, quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that as quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them? Scientists have now developed a promising new method that could help overcome this challenge by measuring the accuracy of quantum simulations and identifying how much uncertainty their predictions contain.

It has been revealed that the technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results. Researchers successfully demonstrated the approach using a quantum simulator with up to 51 qubits in Innsbruck, Austria.

According to recent reports, quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all. However, this progress creates a verification problem. When a simulation is small enough, scientists can compare its results with calculations performed on a conventional computer. As quantum systems grow beyond those limits, that direct comparison becomes impractical, making alternative ways to assess their reliability essential.

A Upcoming Way to Measure Quantum Computing Accuracy.

According to recent reports, the breakthrough comes from an international research team led by Tristan Kraft at the Technical University of Munich and Peter Zoller at the University of Innsbruck and the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, working alongside Barbara Kraus of the Technical University of Munich. The researchers developed a method for experimentally determining how a quantum simulator operates and translating uncertainties in its behavior into measurable limits on the accuracy of its results.

Recent findings suggest that quantum simulators are specialized physical systems designed to reproduce the behavior of other quantum systems. They are especially useful for investigating situations involving large numbers of interacting particles, where the calculations required can swiftly overwhelm even powerful conventional computers.

But quantum experiments are never entirely free from errors. "But no real experiment is perfect," notes Tristan Kraft. "Interactions may turn out differently than expected, the system is influenced by its environment, and measurements are also subject to uncertainties.".

In a recent development, rather than assuming a quantum simulator behaves exactly as intended, the latest approach examines experimental data to determine what is actually happening inside the system. This allows researchers to identify notable interactions and account for disturbances such as fluctuations and noise.

Sources indicate that "From this data, we determine the relevant interactions as well as key influences from fluctuations and noise. We then calculate how the uncertainties in this model affect the simulation results," explains Tristan Kraft. "The quantum simulator thus provides not just a single value, but a result with error margins that quantify its accuracy.".

Successfully Tested on a 51 Qubit Quantum Simulator.

According to recent reports, to evaluate the method, the researchers began with a relatively small quantum system containing ten trapped ions. Because conventional computers can still calculate the behavior of a system of this size, the team could test its reconstructed models and calculated error limits against independent measurements.

Industry observers note that after this initial validation, the researchers expanded their experiments to a chain of 51 trapped ions. The larger demonstration, carried out by a team led by Manoj Joshi and Christian Roos using an ion trap quantum simulator, revealed that the technique could also work with substantially more complex quantum systems.

This represents an vital step toward establishing how trustworthy quantum simulation results are, particularly as quantum devices advance into territory where direct verification with traditional computing methods becomes increasingly difficult.

Extending the Breakthrough to More Complex Quantum Systems.

In a recent development, the next challenge is to bring the technique to two-dimensional quantum simulators. These systems can model more complicated interactions among particles, making them valuable for exploring quantum physics. At the same time, their growing complexity makes their results particularly difficult to confirm using conventional calculations.

"This is particularly notable because classical calculations for such systems become significantly more difficult as the number of particles increases," explains quantum computing pioneer Peter Zoller. "This also makes independent verification of the results increasingly complex, making the question of experimentally determined error limits all the more important.".

The researchers are now adapting their method for the newest generation of two-dimensional quantum simulators, which offer improved precision and can investigate systems containing larger numbers of particles.

Recent findings suggest that looking further ahead, the approach could help scientists establish a more meaningful way to measure quantum advantage, the ability of quantum systems to outperform conventional computers. Instead of comparing machines based only on their processing speed or the size of the problems they can handle, researchers could also examine how accurately each system produces its answers.

In a recent development, "After all, when a classical computer and a quantum simulator tackle the same problem, it's not just a matter of which one delivers a result faster. What's also crucial is which one can solve the problem with a smaller, verifiable margin of error," says Peter Zoller.

This shift could change how progress in quantum computing is evaluated. Future breakthroughs may be judged not simply by how many particles a simulator can model or how swiftly it performs calculations, but by its ability to solve increasingly difficult problems with demonstrably reliable results.

It has been revealed that the findings were published in Physical Review X. The research received support from the Austrian Science Fund (FWF), the German Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, the European Union, BMW, and other funding organizations.

It has been revealed that heartopia, the latest cosy life sim from XD Games, has officially arrived on mobile, right on schedule. If you’ve been keeping up with Heartopia news, you’re likely already aware that the game has pushed back its Steam release to an indeterminate point in 2026.

Doesn’t look like it mattered much, however, as this has already been a big launch on iOS and Android — it probably helps that PC players aren't being entirely left out of the fun, since the game is already available there via XD's own cross-device platform TapTap.

XD Games announced today that Heartopia has reached the top spot on the App Store’s downloads page for free games, and it managed to do so in more than 50 countries and regions worldwide.

Sources indicate that the developer is celebratig by offering players a lot of free stuff. If you're feeling lucky, you’ll find new outfits and furniture in three gacha banners (Gilded Acorn Exhibitions): Polar Hymn, The Frostguard, and Coolplayism.

It has been revealed that XD Games indicates you can expect regular updates to add more content, through Fashionwaves and Festivals. In fact, the first season - Winter Frost - is already penciled in for sometime in late January, and it’s going to add appropriately wintery activities like ice skating and snowman-building.

In February, a My Little Pony collaboration event will kick off, bringing upcoming inspired outfits, and vehicles to the game.

Heartopia is a clever mix of Animal Crossing, and The Sims. It’s a free-to-play life sim where you can create your own character, dress them up, build a home for them (and decorate it), and go about town visiting and playing with other players’ characters.

In a recent development, the game’s main feature is the ability to take on a hobby, and seven of those are available at launch. You can dig deep into each hobby, either alone or with others, and there’s a progression track dedicated to each one.

Whether you’re among the millions who downloaded the game already, or you intend to so soon, we’ve got a set of helpful guides to get you started. You should check out how to unlock and upgrade hobbies in Heartopia first, before you get deep into finding all cooking recipes. And, of course, this wouldn’t be a big game launch without a bunch of Heartopia codes for some free stuff.

Award-Winning Composer And Musician Jon Batiste Talks Ocarina Of Time's Music And Why 'Guile's Theme' Goes With Everything

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jon Batiste has collaborated with the likes of Alicia Keys, Lenny Kravitz, Prince, Stevie Wonder, Willie Nelson, and many more.
  • In a recent development, before I can even ask a question, Batiste begins singing to greet me, then nerds out about my NBA Jam and Street Fighter II cabinets.
  • With The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time delivering some of the most iconic music of all time (and Batiste famously loving the music), it makes sense that Nintendo would bring him out to New York to serve as a special guest at the launch event for the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jon Batiste has collaborated with the likes of Alicia Keys, Lenny Kravitz, Prince, Stevie Wonder, Willie Nelson, and many more. He performed the national anthem at Super Bowl LIX. He's headed up the musical efforts of The Late Show with Stephen Colbert. He's taken home more awards than we can realistically list in this article (including eight Grammys, as well as an Academy Award, a BAFTA Award, and a Golden Globe). But as I sit down with Batiste for a brief conversation about video game music, his energy transcends the Zoom call.

In a recent development, before I can even ask a question, Batiste begins singing to greet me, then nerds out about my NBA Jam and Street Fighter II cabinets. He begins humming the menu music from NBA Jam and reminiscing about all the quarters he pumped into his local Street Fighter cabinet. The Louisiana native and Juilliard School alum has been an ardent gaming enthusiast for nearly three decades, with compositions from games like Sonic the Hedgehog and Final Fantasy VII inspiring his earliest musical endeavors. Spend enough time watching video game music performances on social media, and you'll likely soon find videos of Batiste sitting with famed Final Fantasy composer Nobuo Uematsu, or of Batiste performing gaming music.

With The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time delivering some of the most iconic music of all time (and Batiste famously loving the music), it makes sense that Nintendo would bring him out to New York to serve as a special guest at the launch event for the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2. I sat down with Batiste for a few minutes to chat about his love of video game music, his history with Nintendo, and why "Guile's Theme" from Street Fighter II just goes so well with everything.

Recent findings suggest that ocarina of Time is easily one of the most key video games ever made, and one of the things that makes it so special is the music. What about Ocarina of Time sticks out to you sonically?First off, if you want to get super inside baseball, technical music nerdery, which I love to do, in the compositions, there's a way that major chords and minor chords in... no sevenths, just root, third, fifth. They alternate, and it creates this magic that is, like, it's wistful, and it's simple. It feels ancient, and it feels like it's the music that is going on in your mind as you're generating thoughts and your imagination is churning. And the major chords are happening just after the minors in this contrary motion that's happening, so it feels like the music is going like this: It's going up – major, minor – like [sings the main Legend of Zelda theme song].

So, it's expanding and contracting, which is a musical allegory for the expansion and the openness of the world that Link is in. It's like [Koji Kondo] figured out how to capture the essence of the gameplay, but also the essence of magic and simplicity, which I think is really what makes... that's the music's power! So, you could listen to the music in the game, and you could also listen to it apart from the game and experience that magic.

Are there any tracks in Ocarina of Time that stand out to you as the most musically sophisticated or compositionally impressive?Oh man. Well, I think of it as a suite, so that's what makes it actually... there's nothing that's more or less complex, but the thought to figure out how to make all of the themes be interrelated yet singular. "Song of Storms" is, like, for me, that's a personal favorite. That's why I like to play it. I like to play a lot of the themes. That's how I grew up! I would play the game, and then, I would go to an instrument. Once we played for hours on Nintendo, we'd go and play Nintendo on piano! It was like a trade-off there, you know? I've been doing this since I was about 11 years old.

In a recent development, taking it back to that 11-year-old Jon, talk to me a little bit about your history in general.Okay, so my history with Nintendo goes back to the NES. Christmas morning. Duck Hunt. You remember that? Maybe the first game I ever played. No, the first game I ever played was Donkey Kong, and then Duck Hunt, and then Super Mario Bros. Staples! We're talking about the early '90s. We had a room where I would go – it was my domain – and we had this blue shag carpet, and I would sit back there, and I would basically disappear into the carpet playing Nintendo for hours and hours.

In a recent development, and my mind is kind of... my mind can become a spiral; it can become a tornado. And I realized even then that going into this world of the game, even if I didn't win – it's not about winning or losing – it helps to organize the spiral of my mind and give me ideas and inspiration. So then, I started to get into Street Fighter II when I started to play more communally with my sister and my cousins. Yoko Shimomura, who I also had the pleasure of meeting and collaborating with, she composed incredible themes for each character, and that's when I really started to get a true love for fighting games.

Sources indicate that and then, we would play so many of the Street Fighter franchise. We would play a lot of Final Fight. There were so many things... there was Double Dragon, then we got Mega Man... all these different series. Mega Man X is [an] all-time favorite. And then, here comes The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and that sort of expands the canon while also blending all of the elements: score, combat, the sort of linear quality of, like, a Donkey Kong or Super Mario World, and expanding the world in that way, expanding the canon in that way. Mind-blowing! So,  that sort of solidified my palate in terms of my favorite type of game.

You mentioned Street Fighter II. There's a meme about "Guile's Theme" and how it goes with everything. What about that composition makes it so it has the ability to enhance whatever video you pair it with?Wow! So, it has momentum in a way that is extremely [sings the melody of "Guile's Theme"] ... It draws you in, which is what you want [with] anything that you're starting when you're commencing a journey or watching something. You want it to draw you in, and that kind of pulls you in as that call and response. But it's an immediate announcement with the brass, and then the bass call and response. So, it's automatically giving you this feeling that something's happening, and I've got to pay attention to it! So that's the first step right there. And the tempo is really... it's a great tempo! It almost has the feeling of the great themes from, like, an '80s protagonist that's in a fighting movie. I think that was kind of the archetype. Yoko was probably drawing from that archetype, right? The action-hero archetype.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • As recently revealed, the newly introduced experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT.
  • This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the newly introduced experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside upgrade 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

According to recent reports, the beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the initiative is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

Sources indicate that the Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as swiftly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

Sources indicate that the Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

It has been revealed that the Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two newly introduced additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

#17235. Tech Report: New wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1036 w)

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: New wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1036 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A new wearable patch could offer a surprisingly simple way to improve one of the most notable stages of sleep, without relying on medication or surgery.
  • Recent findings suggest that known as NEUSLeeP, the soft patch attaches to the skin and combines ultrasound stimulation with electrodes that monitor brain activity in real time.
  • REM sleep, short for rapid eye movement sleep, is the stage when most vivid dreaming occurs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new wearable patch could offer a surprisingly simple way to improve one of the most notable stages of sleep, without relying on medication or surgery. Developed by researchers led by the University of Texas at Austin, the device uses gentle ultrasound waves to stimulate regions deep inside the brain, helping people enter REM sleep sooner and spend more time in this restorative stage.

Recent findings suggest that known as NEUSLeeP, the soft patch attaches to the skin and combines ultrasound stimulation with electrodes that monitor brain activity in real time. This allows researchers to influence brain regions involved in sleep while simultaneously tracking how the brain responds.

REM sleep, short for rapid eye movement sleep, is the stage when most vivid dreaming occurs. It also plays an important role in processing emotions, consolidating memories, and adapting to stress. Disturbances in this stage of sleep have been associated with several mental health conditions, making it an important target for new treatments.

Recent findings suggest that "This is the first time we've been able to noninvasively target deep brain regions involved in REM sleep, while simultaneously monitoring brain activity," said Kai Wing "Kevin" Tang, a recent UT biomedical engineering Ph.D. graduate who led the research effort.

"Our skin-attached NEUSLeeP patch opens up latest possibilities for understanding sleep and treating sleep disorders in home settings," added Huiliang "Evan" Wang, assistant professor in the Cockrell School of Engineering's Department of Biomedical Engineering. Wang supervised Tang's research and served as the principal investigator (PI) overseeing the project.

Sleep Patch Helps People Reach REM Sleep 43 Minutes Faster.

The early results suggest that the technology can make a measurable difference in how people experience REM sleep.

In a study involving 28 participants, published in Nature Communications, people using the patch entered REM sleep an average of 43 minutes sooner and spent approximately 16 additional minutes in that stage.

Sources indicate that these improvements were observed in both healthy sleepers and participants experiencing certain sleep difficulties. The volunteers also reported that the patch was comfortable to wear, with minimal adverse effects.

Unlike medications that affect the body more broadly, NEUSLeeP is designed to deliver stimulation to specific brain regions involved in sleep regulation. It uses ultrasound, a form of sound energy with frequencies beyond human hearing, to reach areas beneath the surface of the brain without requiring an invasive procedure.

The findings are encouraging, although the relatively small study means that larger trials will be needed to determine how consistently the technology works and whether its benefits persist over time.

Potential Benefits for Stress and Emotional Health.

The researchers also found evidence that the patch's effects may extend beyond increasing REM sleep.

Industry observers note that among healthy participants, ultrasound stimulation improved heart rate variability, a measure of the natural differences in time between consecutive heartbeats. This measurement provides insight into how the body's nervous system responds to stress and adjusts to changing conditions.

Recent findings suggest that brain imaging revealed changes in neural circuits involved in emotional processing. Together, these findings suggest that improving REM sleep through targeted stimulation could potentially support emotional regulation and the ability to cope with stress.

"REM sleep is not just about dreaming -- it's about emotional reset and stress adaptation," explained Gregory Fonzo, assistant professor in the Dell Medical School's Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences and one of the project's co-PIs. "By enhancing REM, we may help people better cope with stress and improve their overall well-being.".

These possibilities are especially interesting because REM sleep disturbances have been linked to depression, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

According to recent reports, current approaches to sleep problems often involve medication or behavioral therapy. Although these treatments can be effective, medications may produce unwanted side effects, and existing approaches do not always directly address the biological processes responsible for disrupted REM sleep.

Recent findings suggest that A device capable of influencing those processes without drugs or surgery could therefore offer an additional treatment option. However, the researchers have not yet established whether NEUSLeeP can improve symptoms of mental health disorders.

A Fresh Direction for Treating Insomnia and PTSD.

Building on the initial findings, the research team intends to conduct larger clinical trials to confirm the patch's effects and investigate its potential use in people with PTSD, depression, and chronic insomnia.

Sources indicate that beyond treating sleep disorders, the technology could eventually support sleep monitoring at home and provide scientists with a new way to study how deep brain regions influence sleep. Researchers also envision personalized therapies that could be adjusted to individual sleep patterns and needs.

Sources indicate that "Our vision is a future where patients with mental health disorders can optimize their sleep with a noninvasive and safe treatment," said Vincent Mysliwiec, M.D., a professor at UT Health San Antonio, a leading expert in sleep disorders, and another co-PI on the project. "This technology could help millions of people get the restorative sleep they need.".

Industry observers note that the team is already taking steps toward making NEUSLeeP available beyond the research setting. Working with the university's commercialization unit, Discovery to Impact, the researchers are exploring how to bring the device to market and have filed a patent application covering the technology.

If future studies confirm the early results, this wearable ultrasound patch could become a valuable new tool for improving REM sleep and potentially addressing conditions associated with poor sleep.

Sources indicate that other members of the research team include William D. Moscoso-Barrera, Mengxia Yu, Mengmeng Yao, Jinmo Jeong, Ilya Pyatnitskiy, Anakaren Romero Lozano, Jiachen Wang, Ju-Chun Hsieh, Tony Sungjin Chae, Daniel Song, Julieta Garcia, Rithvik Mittapalli, and Adam Bush of the Department of Biomedical Engineering; Benjamin Baird of the College of Natural Sciences' Department of Psychology; and Wynn Legon of Virginia Tech's Fralin Biomedical Research Institute.

Materials provided by University of Texas at Austin. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This week and weekend is all about the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, one of the few games I feel deserves the title of masterpiece. And the remake is really well done! I got every heart piece, every Gold Skulltala, the Goron Sword, and the biggest pouch for every one of my items over the course of the review... but I am contemplating jumping right back in for another go.

Sources indicate that we also revealed our next cover and in case you missed the announcement it is... pause for effect... Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis! It's an awesome cover that celebrates the history of Lara Croft, and along with a cover story on the game, we also have a substantial retrospective on the series. I highly recommend subscribing to get your glitch if you haven't already.

But it wasn't all just Zelda and Tomb Raider this week. Below you will find a list of weekend play recommendations, but before that... some of our biggest stories of the week.

It has been revealed that we have been writing a lot about The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time remake this week because it is one of 2026's most exciting games, and it's real good. The remake is not particularly surprising. It mostly sticks to the trajectory of the original game, but there is a reason it is considered one of the best games of all time. It also looks and plays amazing.

You can read the full review here (or watch the video above), but we also have a big interview with the game's producers (one of whom worked on the original Ocarina of Time, and one who directed Breath of the Wild among many other Zelda games), some details about the Easter Eggs that did and did not make it into the remake, and a very handy tip for the game if you happen to be playing with a Switch 2 Pro controller.

World of Warcraft: Forever is out now and it’s a great time to jump into the revamped and expanded version of a project that changed online games forever back in 2004. A thousand newly introduced quests, multiple new zones, countless revamps, and an impressively stunning visual overhaul make it the perfect time to jump in for anyone who’s ever been curious to explore Azeroth.

It has been revealed that 2022's Escape Academy was a sneaky little puzzle game that surprised me and its sequel released this week. Taking place in a school obsessed with puzzles, you play as a student who must make their way through a series of escape rooms. The puzzles are clever, and the setting is charming, but the secret weapon is the local, split-screen co-op. Solving puzzles together is fun especially when one player needs to look at one section of a room to help dictate a solution on the other side of the room. My wife and I both love video games, but rarely play co-op games together just because of our disparate, individual tastes. But Escape Room is one we enjoyed together and we're so far enjoying the sequel. My only complaint so far is... I wish it ran a little better.

While we collectively use the term here for the sake of familiarity, I’m always a bit hesitant in my own mind to label a game under the wide banner of “Metroidvania.” In part, that’s because I think the two referenced games (Metroid and Castlevania: Symphony of the Night) are actually more different than they might appear at first glance. Gloomsoft’s recent release, Moadra, recognizes that distinction, crafting a game that draws heavy inspiration from the specific tradition of Super Metroid, even while presenting an intriguing and atmospheric fiction that is great fun to discover. In movement, actions, and exploration, Moadra feels remarkably similar to  the best of the 2D Metroid games. A scanning tool also leans into the Metroid inspirations, revealing details about the weird alien world you’re navigating. If you’ve been hungry for a game that scratches that particular itch of sci-fi gear/ability-gated exploration, I think you’ll find a lot to love in this game.

I get the Marvel fatigue we've all been experiencing. There are a lot of games and a lot of movies and a lot of TV reveals and many are good, but lately most feel like homework. For those reasons, you'd be forgiven for dismissing the 2021 Guardians of the Galaxy game, but I promise you it is good. For one, it is standalone. It does not directly tie to any specific Marvel media. No homework necessary. And for two, it's just a really good game with an affecting story and a unique take on the characters that most of us met for the first time in the movies. And, for the BioWare fans out there mourning the loss of Mass Effect, this game has some Mass Effect energy. It's available on Switch 2 this week and I happily recommend it, especially if you missed it five years ago.

This exclusively two-player board game features a fun mix of activities. You act as both a dungeon architect, and an adventurer delving into stated dungeons. Each player creates their own version of a challenging dungeon filled with traps, monsters, and treasures.

According to recent reports, but you’re also forced to take on the dangers of your opponent’s crafted dungeon, to see who manages to come out on top. If you have fond memories of the hidden-info nature of old games like Battleship, but you want some greater strategic depth and fantasy flavor thrown in, this one is a great pick.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that link has faced countless monsters, found 100 Skulltulas more than once, and saved Hyrule more times than we can count. But after all these years, one of the most recognizable things about the hero has remained largely unchanged: he rarely speaks.

That might be why a tiny detail in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake has caught the attention of fans, as it appears to give Link an actual spoken line.

The discovery was recently shared by The Legend of Zelda Updates on X (formerly Twitter), which posted a clip showing Link briefly speaking Japanese during a scene with Princess Zelda.

And while it's certainly not a lengthy conversation or a dramatic speech, hearing the usually silent protagonist say something out loud is still a pretty big deal for the franchise. Here, take a look by yourself (and don’t forget to turn up the volume, of course):.

Watch the clip shared by The Legend of Zelda Updates on X.

According to recent reports, this moment takes place during the game's closing sequence, as Link and Zelda attempt to escape the collapsing castle. As the hero takes hold of the princess in his arms, he can be heard saying "さあ" (pronounced "Sā"), a Japanese expression that can be translated as "come on" or "let's go," depending on the context.

There's a catch, though: the line can only be heard when playing with Japanese audio! Players using other language options won't get to hear Link deliver this little piece of dialogue, making it an especially easy detail to miss – I, for instance, played it in English and Portuguese, and I can confirm that he was silent on both.

This was quickly shared on gaming forums and social media, since it appears that the Ocarina of Time remake may have broken one of the franchise’s biggest traditions of having a silent protagonist! But it is also worth pointing out that this isn't exactly the first time Link has ever spoken. The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker, for example, features a brief “Come on!” from the hero when players call companions and even a “Meow” – and I don’t know about you, but for me, that’s pretty close to this time’s “let’s go” in the remake.

This moment takes place during the game's closing sequence, as Link and Zelda attempt to escape the collapsing castle. As the hero takes hold of the princess in his arms, he can be heard saying "さあ" (pronounced "Sā"), a Japanese expression that can be translated as "come on" or "let's go," depending on the context.

According to recent reports, still, Link has largely remained a silent protagonist throughout the series, with his thoughts and responses usually left to the player's imagination. So, interestingly, the remake has decided to tackle that idea again, and only in the Japanese dub. And it doesn't suddenly turn Link into a talkative protagonist, nor does it suggest that Nintendo is abandoning one of the series' most recognizable traditions. It's just a small surprise that fans probably weren't expecting to hear!

And honestly, I can understand why this has caught everyone's attention. After nearly four decades of adventures, hearing Link say even a couple of syllables feels strangely significant. Whether this was an intentional creative decision or simply a small addition to the Japanese performance, it's another example of how even the tiniest changes can get Zelda fans talking!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In their (slightly belated) newly introduced years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are at the moment working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

According to recent reports, this, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Recent findings suggest that understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s fresh ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we blueprint for today, tomorrow, and the future.”.

Recent findings suggest that as for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of newly introduced Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Sources indicate that future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that dota 2 will return to the Riyadh-hosted Esports World Cup in 2027, though dates, format and prize money are still to come.
  • According to recent reports, dota 2’s place at Esports World Cup 2027 was unveiled without dates, a prize pool, a format or any invited teams.
  • The 2026 tournament had originally been planned for Riyadh before it was moved to Paris on 20 May 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that dota 2 will return to the Riyadh-hosted Esports World Cup in 2027, though dates, format and prize money are still to come. The title has never been won twice, and its prize pool has fallen at every edition so far.

According to recent reports, dota 2’s place at Esports World Cup 2027 was unveiled without dates, a prize pool, a format or any invited teams. The whole event is listed for July to August 2027.

The 2026 tournament had originally been planned for Riyadh before it was moved to Paris on 20 May 2026.

The first edition, Riyadh Masters 2024, carried a US$5,000,000 prize pool. In 2025 Team Spirit took US$1,000,000 from a US$3,000,000 pool in a 16-team event. The 2026 tournament ran from 7 to 19 July with 24 teams. That field was eight teams larger than a year earlier.

The winner still takes a large share. PARIVISION collected US$750,000, or 37.5% of the pool, plus 1,000 Club Championship points. Runners-up BetBoom Team received US$340,000 and 750 points, Liquipedia reported.

It has been revealed that those points feed into a larger prize. In 2026 the Club Championship paid US$30 million across the top 24 clubs. The champion club received US$7 million from an overall event prize pool of US$75 million. AG.AL won it with 5,300 points, stopping Team Falcons from winning a third title in a row. For organisations weighing the cost of a Dota 2 roster, that club prize is part of the calculation.

Not every club is staying. Falcons released all five players from the roster that won The International 2025, according to Timesaver.gg.

It has been revealed that no club or player has won the event’s Dota 2 title more than once. Each of the three editions went to a different club with a different roster. Gaimin Gladiators beat Team Liquid in the 2024 final. A year later, Team Spirit swept Team Falcons 3-0. As the 2026 champions, PARIVISION now get the first chance to defend the title.

PVISION are your Dota 2 at EWC26 Champions! 👏 pic.twitter.com/34U67Oaj7G.

— Esports World Cup (@EWC_EN) July 20, 2026.

Their rivals arrive in form. Team Spirit went out of the 2026 event before the final. A month later, they won The International 2026 in Shanghai. Yatoro and Collapse became the first players to win three Internationals. Team Yandex finished third at both the 2026 Esports World Cup and The International. After signing ATF, they won PGL Wallachia Season 9 and BLAST SLAM VIII.

It has been revealed that the route into the event is taking shape. The organiser’s Road to EWC qualifier programme for 2027 aims to involve 1.8 million players across more than 400 events. Qualifier slots for each game will be revealed later. Counter-Strike 2, already confirmed for both 2027 and 2028, will hold a 32-team event in Riyadh from 20 July to 1 August 2027.
