General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gamesradar ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: D&D World of Warcraft designer hopes "to push the rest of the design team forward" with new skills learned from making this book

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1511 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • During Fresh York Comic Con, I sat down with Wizards of the Coast Principal Game Designer James Wyatt to talk about the upcoming D&D: World of Warcraft book.
  • The process of translating Azeroth to one of the best tabletop RPGs was no easy feat, and it became quite clear that the team really pushed their design philosophies in latest directions with D&D World of Warcraft.
  • GamesRadar+: So just walk me through the project, because there's obviously so much you could draw from World of Warcraft.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

During Fresh York Comic Con, I sat down with Wizards of the Coast Principal Game Designer James Wyatt to talk about the upcoming D&D: World of Warcraft book. This is the first of the Dungeons & Dragons Universes Beyond expansions, blending the familiar characters and locations of Warcraft with D&D rulesets.

The process of translating Azeroth to one of the best tabletop RPGs was no easy feat, and it became quite clear that the team really pushed their design philosophies in latest directions with D&D World of Warcraft. We spoke about the process of bringing Azeroth to life in a whole new way, translating original World of Warcraft Classes like Evoker to D&D, and about the shared experience of tabletop role-playing games.

GamesRadar+: So just walk me through the project, because there's obviously so much you could draw from World of Warcraft. Is the Lich King (pictured on the cover) the main villain here?

Sources indicate that james Wyatt, principal game designer: That's just one of many possibilities. So there is this map pack that comes with a digital code to download an Icecrown Citadel adventure. You can take level 16 characters and brave Icecrown Citadel and get all the way up to level 20 by the time you reach the frozen throne. But that's just one of the many ingredients we are providing for your cooking experience.

D&D World of Warcraft is up for pre-order at Amazon now, where you can also pick up a WoW-themed Dungeon Master's Screen and a Map Pack for the Icecrown Citadel adventure.

We lay out the Alliance versus Horde. Here's the Burning Legion, the Dragonflight, the Elemental Lords, the Old Gods, the Scourge, and for each one [...] we talked about how to implement these themes through a 20 level campaign and beyond. In fact, there's an endgame section for each one. So that is sort of like your tasting menu of ingredients you can add into the campaign and mix however you want.

Recent findings suggest that I talked myself into the idea in my last interview of running a campaign that really focuses on the Alliance Horde conflict. Where you've got a mixed group of characters from both factions who are trying to bring that conflict to an end and having diplomacy and clandestine meetings and subterfuge and intrigue. I think that even a D&D player who's not into WoW can find inspiration here and stuff to throw in a campaign and help build your own world.

According to recent reports, dungeons play a huge role in D&D World of Warcraft. What was the process of figuring out how to translate them?

We mostly tried to translate the maps as faithfully as we could to how they appear in the game. I spent a lot of time particularly working on Ice Crown Citadel, just having my high level Druid sneaking around invisible to see how all the pieces fit together and what the building looks like inside and everything. A lot of time flying around the top trying to figure it out as well.

In a recent development, but I think of the dungeon presentations here as very similar to what we did with the half page adventures in the Dungeon Master's guide. It's just a little bit of text on the map and here we're refreshing that a little bit. We take the map and we put pins in and say, okay, here's the dungeon bosses. Here are the things we know you're going to do and the rest we give you some description of what's here, the kinds of creatures you might encounter. But really, that's where the chaos and the fun and improvisation are happening. There's a lot of room for players to do the crazy things that players do because we all know that no plan survives contact with the players. So what's going to happen there?

In a recent development, when you're developing stat lines for something like Illidan, what's that process look like? You're balancing for an entirely different format.

I've been using the word paraphrase a lot. It's not translating from one game to another. What does that feel like? What's the sense that it's trying to convey?

[For] the length of time the boss is going to survive, we tried to give them some survivability obviously. And Illidan's Challenge Rating 24, so he's going to be tough for even a level 20 party, but figuring out those iconic abilities are what is going to make this feel like that fight against Illidan in Lost Temple and how we translate that or express that in D&D.

Recent findings suggest that has everything from WoW been carried over? Have you found a way to work dailies into this, for example?

In a recent development, no, and that's actually one of the things that we talk about in the adventure chapter. There's tons of ideas in WoW that you could easily port over into D&D. But we spell out a couple of things to watch out for because they are different games, and not all of those quests ported over are going to be fun at the tabletop. If you want to wander around The Barrens collecting Zhevra Hooves… no thanks. It's going to take us 20 minutes to kill one Zhevra as opposed to five seconds. That matters. So we talked about avoiding the grind. Having characters' actions make a difference in the world, make a lasting impact on the world, letting them occupy the spotlight and not other characters.

In a recent development, A mount in an MMO is a victory lap. It's the "I did this thing and I've accomplished something major." Is that the thought process with mounts in this, where it's just a reward? Because in D&D, you could just ask, "Can I go buy a horse?" And your DM might be like, "Yeah.".

Recent findings suggest that exactly. That whole aspect of prestige, of accomplishment, is much harder to reproduce in any way in a D&D game. So when you kill the Lich King, he does drop the Rains of Invincible, so you can have that special mount. That's pretty cool.

Recent findings suggest that but yeah, you can also just go and buy a Pandarian Dragon Turtle… So that element is still there. It's just not really in the forefront.

It has been revealed that it's not a game of individual achievement. Anything that you did at the table, you did with your friends and so you all shared that glory. Travel speed is not a constant frustration for a D&D player the way it is for an MMO player that you need to overcome.

It has been revealed that what do you think is one lesson you learned from this entire experience? What do you think is something that's going to stick with you?

In a recent development, there's a lot of little things in terms of design where I hope my goal is to push the rest of the design team forward on some things that I learned from doing this. I'm really curious about the way we did the Death Knight and the Demon Hunter as what we call a Hero Class using WoW language, a subclass that alters your base features.

According to recent reports, there's some interesting potential there that we could use in core D&D as well. I don't know yet what that's going to look like, what classes those might be, no idea, but it's something I want to explore. Pushing our monster design forward similarly, but even little things like the Druid's specific wild shaped forms. We already did this for a future book with a Cataclysm Druid or whatever it's called now where you take on a kaiju form basically. We used the same technology. I pulled out these stat blocks from the draft as it existed then and stated this is the model you should follow.

Industry observers note that that's what we do as a team. We're constantly pushing our design forward. I think this book does that in a wide spectrum of things. The cool thing about it is it's almost an Everything book with something for everybody here, just focused around Azeroth.

Dungeons & Dragons: World of Warcraft launches on November 17, 2026.

That Cataclysm Druid Wyatt mentions could be a part of the upcoming Dark Sun reboot, which is due to launch early next year.

  • The departures follow swiftly on from Smoggy’s move to Bilibili Gaming.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EDward Gaming have lost captain nobody and CHICHOO, two days after releasing Smoggy to Bilibili Gaming. The VCT China partner team must now rebuild before the China Kickoff in Hangzhou in January.

EDward Gaming have parted ways with CHICHOO and captain nobody, two pillars of the side that won VALORANT Champions 2024. Both players left the VCT China partner team on the same day. EDG unveiled both exits on Weibo. Their exits end a five-year spell at the organisation.

The departures follow swiftly on from Smoggy’s move to Bilibili Gaming. Within a week, three players had gone from the EDG roster. No replacements have been named.

Wang ‘nobody’ Senxu joined EDG on 7 September 2021. He served as the team’s captain and in-game leader. He had started out as the side’s Initiator before taking on those leadership duties. CHICHOO, whose full name is Wan Shunzhi, played the Controller role. Alongside CHICHOO, he formed the core of the only Chinese team to win Champions. That title, sealed on 25 August 2024, made EDG the first organisation from China, and from Asia, to lift the trophy. The team’s total winnings stand at roughly $1,592,287.

Industry observers note that the pair were still central to the side in 2026. At Masters London, CHICHOO and nobody each played 12 maps. Their average combat scores were 179 and 184 respectively. EDG finished third in London and earned $125,000. Their run ended with a 0-3 defeat to Leviatán in the lower bracket final on 20 June 2026.

Where nobody goes next is not yet confirmed. Sheep Esports reported, citing sources, that he is expected to join Trace Esports for 2027. Trace’s Kai and deLb are remarked to be under contract until the end of 2027. If that move happens, nobody and Smoggy would both start the latest season with different organisations.

The timing is awkward for EDG. The organisation was named a VCT partner team on 21 October, on a two-year contract. That deal now begins with a heavily changed roster.

Sources indicate that the China Kickoff is an S-Tier LAN event. It is organised by TJ Sports, Hero Esports and Riot Games. The league’s partner sides make up eight places in the field, with the remaining four split evenly between visiting teams and open qualifier entrants. EDG will need a settled line-up in place to compete there.

Industry observers note that fortunately, an enhancement is already in the works to add Joy-Con 2 mouse controls to this version of the game. These controls can be accessed right now in the closed beta build.

According to recent reports, this includes the ability to use mouse controls with either the left or right Joy-Con, and you can also customise settings, such as cursor and camera sensitivity. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In what feels a fairly cheeky move during a time when memory shortages have infamously made it pretty much impossible to buy a decently powerful new graphics card without spending approximately a gazillion pounds/dollars/dollarpounds, Nvidia have decided to put out a Steam demo that allows folks to re-live the feeling of unboxing a ludicrously expensive graphics card in 2006.

In a recent development, the demo, dubbed GeForce 8800 GTX - 20 Years of a Legend, has been developed by Dylan Browne. He previously made Through The Ages, a "real-time high end graphical cinematic that takes us on a nostalgic journey through three of NVIDIA's iconic GPUs" which is also on Steam for reasons.

Recent findings suggest that the GeForce 8800 GTX demo, as you might've guessed, is a tribute to that specific card in the form of a tech demo simulating what it was like to unbox one in a mid-2000s bedroom. Seriously, there's a copy of Crysis on the desk so you know this is the domain of a true devotee to the best graphics available in around 2007.

Sources indicate that "Step into a 2006-era PC gaming room, unbox the GeForce 8800 GTX, inspect it up close, and install it in an era-accurate PC tower," the demo's description declares. "Explore nods to GeForce history and hidden easter eggs as DLSS 4.5 with Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, Ray Reconstruction, path tracing, and Mega Geometry bring the nostalgic setting to life. From holding the card to the glow of the monitor, rediscover a moment in PC gaming history - or experience it for the first time!".

Industry observers note that as the GeForce 8800 GTX was a top-line card that cost $599 on release in 2006 - about $1,000 in today's money if the online inflation calculator I've just used is on the money - this isn't really a 'we know cards are ludicrously expensive right now, but here's a reminder of when you used to be able to actually afford to unbox one' sort of demo. It is at least a free way to virtually experience having blown a chunk of your savings on something that can render really sexy textures without the existential dread of doing so in real life.

Industry observers note that well, I say that, I've just noticed the minimum requirements for the demo note that you'll need an RTX 4070 card. So, depending on your current setup, this might well be a case of Nvidia offering the chance to render unboxing a card you couldn't afford in 2006 via a card you can't afford in 2026.

Sources indicate that is that about the best we can all hope for in 2026? Probably.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content.
  • It has been revealed that as discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content.
  • The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the new maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it plans to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

It has been revealed that as discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a big component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the new maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios says the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

The blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of significant maps as Battlefield 6 currently is.

Another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. Interestingly, there appears to be some sort of mechanic unique to Contaminated that the developer also wants to evaluate.

More Labs sessions are planned, including one that will show off latest gameplay tools and vehicles. The AH-6 Little Bird helicopter was specifically namedropped, which makes sense given that it’s going to be part of Season 2’s content.

Battlefield Labs sessions will also extend beyond the biggest-ticket items of maps and vehicles. BF Studios said we should expect tests of upcoming features, like the Aircraft Radar, as part of a list of other air combat updates.

Ground vehicles, and they way the various rockets interact with them, will also be evaluated in a different session, with specific adjustments planned for RPGs and TOWs. And, of course, the work to improve and perfect hit reg remains ongoing, and future tweaks will go through Labs first.

It has been revealed that there’s even more exciting news for fans of big maps, as the blog post also confirmed that Battlefield 4’s Golmud Railway is right now in the works, planned to go live in a future season. Golmud Railway will show up early in Labs, and you can expect it to evolve over multiple sessions.

According to recent reports, for context, when it does arrive in Battlefield 6, Golmud Railway will be the largest map in the game, which is saying something. Though the map is beloved by vehicle players, it has its challenges elsewhere, and BF Studios notes it will be looking at all that when it creates the BF6, emphasising that it won’t be a simple port of the BF4 original.

In a recent development, finally, the post throws a bone to Redsec battle royale players still waiting for a Solo mode. BF Studios continues to test the idea internally, but it’s taking a while. Needless to say, there are so many aspects that need to be considered. Game pace, balance, player survivability, match flow just to name a few.

Sources indicate that redsec BR was built with squads in mind, so that task is extra challenging. Though the developer didn’t say when we can expect Solos to arrive in Labs, players will get a chance to experience it before it enters the live game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new dawn beckons with GTA 6, and players of the previous Grand Theft Auto are planning a goodbye for the industry-defining juggernaut. To celebrate Rockstar's sequel finally arriving, GTA 5 fans are going to have one last ride around Los Santos, in tribute to a game that's refused to slow down for 13 years.

Recent findings suggest that the event is known as The Last Ride, and it'll take place on November 18, the eve of GTA 6's arrival. CraftizyTV is behind the original idea, posting about it on TIkTok. "For a lot of us, this game wasn't just a game, it was years of memories," they say. Players in GTA Online are going to get together and make a final spin through the streets, valleys, and highways of Grand Theft Auto 5's map before jumping into to the next installment.

Rather than causing more chaos, this will be a subdued jaunt by design. There will be no crime or police chases (surely). You'll start at Los Santos International Airport, and route through Del Perro Pier and Paleto Bay to finish on Mount Chiliad for a stunning view.

It has been revealed that the idea is to admire the craft of what's been a fixture of many people's lives for well over a decade at this point. YouTuber Dezoh puts it perfectly in the video above. "I was 13 or 14 years old when [GTA 5] came out, I'm now 27," he indicates, recording himself partaking in his own solo lap of the sunny hills of Los Santos.

There will be many such cases. The whole landscape of streaming, YouTube, and games media has changed drastically since then. GTA 5 is older than Twitch Plays Pokémon, even.

According to recent reports, some are livestreaming their final hours winding through the cross-generational behemoth. As of me writing this, you can catch the immensely popular GTA 5 and GTA Online video creator The Gaming Gorilla knockin' around, enjoying a life-changing game for what'll likely be one of the last times.

It is weird that GTA 6 is finally here. But it's a reminder all things change and move on. Cherish what you have while you have it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that after weeks of waiting, Arc Raiders developer Embark has officially unveiled the first few months of the game’s 2026 roadmap. The plan is split into four months, covering January to April, collectively dubbed Escalation.

In a recent development, we’re expecting a content revision each month, with the majority of the biggest additions happening on the game’s existing maps. There is, however, at least one upcoming map in the works, but it won’t be here until sometime in April.

It has been revealed that while we wait for that, Arc Raiders is going to go through several events and other in-game changes, some more meaningful (and exciting) than others. January looks to be the lightest so far, which makes sense given that it’s just a week or so from ending.

January’s chapter is titled Headwinds, kicking off on January 27. This segment will see the addition of a fresh matchmaking option for players above level 40 - at or near the game’s endgame. We’re also expecting a new Map Condition, and a new Player Project for everyone to contribute to.

It has been revealed that things start getting interesting in February, when Shrouded Sky will begin. This chapter brings three exciting additions to Arc Raiders. There will be a latest Map Condition, new Arc Threat, and the start of another Player Project.

Interestingly, we’re going to see some sort of map revision during the month, but Embark didn’t share anymore details. The next Raider Deck will also deploy in February, alongside a fresh Expedition Window.

The Flashpoint chapter begins in March, when we’re expecting another latest Map Condition, one more new Arc Threat, as well as another Player Project. March’s most interesting addition is an upgrade to everyone’s trusty rooster friend, Scrappy.

Finally, April is when the significant guns come out, because that’s when the first new map of 2026 will arrive in Arc Raiders. With it, comes a new large Arc, which is to be expected. A new Map Condition will debut then, too, likely starting off on the new map.

That’s pretty much it, but seeing as we’re just one day away from the start of the January stage, things are about to get exciting again in Arc Raiders.

  • Industry observers note that sentinels called keiko ‘bloody brilliant’ in its announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sentinels have signed Briton Georgio 'keiko' Sanassy from NRG as the final starter in their 2027 VCT Americas lineup. The move pairs him again with former NRG teammate brawk as Sentinels try to return to international events after missing them all in 2026.

In a recent development, the Sentinels lineup for 2027 now reads johnqt, brawk, OXY, canezerra and keiko. Zellsis rounds out the group as sixth man. He came back to the organisation on 7 November in that role and as a content creator. Contract lengths were not disclosed.

Industry observers note that sentinels called keiko ‘bloody brilliant’ in its announcement. Riot’s VALORANT Esports account then shared the news and described him as ‘the finishing touch’ on the lineup.

Sheep Esports first reported the move on 8 November, citing sources, and mentioned keiko was expected to play controller. The same report had brawk on initiator and johnqt on sentinel.

It has been revealed that the signing ends a rapid rebuild. OXY arrived on 2 November and brawk a day later. canezerra followed on 6 November. Four days after that, cortezia and Reduxx were released.

Only a few hours before joining Sentinels, brawk had ruled out staying at NRG.

Recent findings suggest that keiko’s NRG spell ran from 12 November 2025 to 21 October 2026. He finished third at Masters Santiago 2026. He also placed third in both VCT Americas Stage 1 and Stage 2. At Champions 2026 he finished joint fifth to sixth.

Industry observers note that that spell ended once Champions was over. NRG told him he would not be kept for the following year, keiko said on X on 21 October. He was then free to look for a upcoming team as a restricted free agent.

Sentinels reached no international event in 2026. The team went out of that year’s Kickoff in the bottom four. It then missed the playoffs in both Stage 1 and Stage 2. Adding a player with that run of results is consistent with a side trying to close the gap quickly.

keiko was born on 12 September 2003. He grew up in and around London. He played competitive Fortnite before switching to VALORANT. His VALORANT career began at UK sides WYLDE, from May to August 2022, and BONK, from October to December 2022. He then joined Apeks from January to November 2023. That year he won the Challengers Rising Stars award. Team Liquid followed, from November 2023 to November 2025. His move to Sentinels places a British player at the centre of a rebuilt Americas contender.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No doubt eager as peas to help pay off EA's billions in debt, battle royale shooter Apex Legends is set to run another of its intellectual propertytastic crossover events. This one, starting on November 10th, stars Godzilla, of Godzilla Minus Zero, Godzilla vs. Kong, Godzilla (1954), Godzilla 2000: Millennium, Godzilla (1998), Son of Godzilla, and Godzilla (2014). I might be missing some.

In a recent development, besides a profitable range of weapon and character skins, most of which appear to have hot glue gunned an 70-year film franchise's worth of dorsal fins all over themselves, the King of the Monsters himself will show up on the game's Storm Point map. He does at least have more than a background cameo: he'll occasionally blast an area with Legend-melting atomic breath, though brave souls who risk the danger zone can score a custom Devotion LMG with a unique heat ray attack of its own.

Sources indicate that worth noting also that the character skins are each based on a certain 'zilla movie, though as our freelance news writer and associate Large Lizard Cinema expert Ashley isn't working today, I'm not sure which of these are from hits and which are the duds. Walking wallhack motherfucker Bloodhound gets the newest fashion, their skin being inspired by Minus Zero, while my personal favourite Scottish scientist Horizon gets duds based on Big G in Godzilla vs. Destoroyah. Octane's skin is taken from... something called a Jet Jaguar? Google suggests this may in fact be elite Godzilla knowledge, something I clearly lack.

Regardless, and with the understanding that a lot of effort goes into these crossovers, I still kinda wish they didn't exist? Even putting aside basic game-playing problems with how, for example, wacky skins interfere with Legend silhouettes – you couldn't pay me to initiate a fight against a full team of near-identical Gundampeople - it's just icky to have an otherwise sharp, smart, at times fiercely competitive battle royale turned into an animated billboard for a few days.

Recent findings suggest that besides, Apex already has its own kaiju: the sleepy, pacifist Leviathans that innocently wandered into the King's Canyon map for a few of the earlier seasons. I consider these much better Friend Material than Godzilla, on the grounds that they'd only kill you by accident, and it was usually your own fault - by wandering under their briefly raised megahooves - anyway.

#17193. 10 Party Members I Benched Immediately (and Still Feel Guilty About)

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2066 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

10 Party Members I Benched Immediately (and Still Feel Guilty About)

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2066 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I have a complicated relationship with the party menu.
  • According to recent reports, it is rarely personal.
  • Baldur’s Gate 3 is a very interesting case when it comes to companions: a lot of them start out really, really unlikable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I have a complicated relationship with the party menu. In any RPG with more companions than party slots, somebody has to stay behind at camp, and whilst I would love to tell you that I rotate everyone fairly, that would be a lie. Some characters get benched within minutes of joining, and most of them never make it back out.

According to recent reports, it is rarely personal. Some of them are too slow, some arrive too late, and some simply have the misfortune of standing next to a character I like more. I do still feel guilty about every single one of them, though, so let’s take a look at ten party members I benched immediately, and why I’m still a little bit sorry about it.

Baldur’s Gate 3 is a very interesting case when it comes to companions: a lot of them start out really, really unlikable. Then you get to know them and their motivations, and it suddenly becomes quite understandable why they act the way that they do. Larian Studios did that so well that benching anyone feels a little bit like abandoning a friend.

Gale is the one I leave at camp regardless. I don’t mind his storyline at all, but I simply don’t enjoy the way wizards work, with every spell slot spent bringing you one step closer to yet another long rest. I usually play a Warlock myself, and having a reliable cantrip like Eldritch Blast means that I never have to worry about that kind of balancing act, especially early on.

It also doesn’t help that there are plenty of companions I like a lot more. Gale’s personality is just a bit goofy for my taste, and whilst I did keep him around for one full playthrough to properly get to know him and his story, I have never felt the need to repeat that. He is a perfectly lovely man. He’s just a perfectly lovely man who waits at camp.

According to recent reports, blue mages have always been one of the more interesting concepts in Final Fantasy. Their magic tends to be really powerful, since there has to be a reason to use them over your regular black, white and even red mages, and that usually means they go from being a bit weak to being suddenly wildly overpowered. Kimahri should be exactly that kind of character.

According to recent reports, the problem is that his blue magic is tied to his Overdrive. He learns enemy abilities with Lancet, but can only use them as his Ronso Rage, and whilst there are ways to charge Overdrives faster later on, it makes him awkward for a large part of the game. Everyone else in the party already has a clearly defined role, too, and Kimahri sits in his own odd little corner of the Sphere Grid without one.

According to recent reports, now, I tend to 100% every Final Fantasy, so he does get used eventually. If I’m simply building a party, though, he is the last character on my mind, which is a shame. Truth be told, the story doesn’t help, either: as Yuna’s guardian, he barely speaks early on, and that makes it hard to form an emotional connection with him. His character design is absolutely sick, mind you.

It has been revealed that sharla is a trap, and I say that with love. When she first joins in Xenoblade Chronicles, she is a pretty good character: a dedicated healer with some decent ether arts, at a point where you have nobody else to bench her for. That is precisely where the problem starts.

Because she feels essential early on, you keep her, even as better options join. She deals next to no damage, though, which means that fights take longer, and longer fights mean that you take more damage. All of that damage then gets healed by Sharla, who ends up looking far more useful than she actually is.

According to recent reports, I fell for it on my first playthrough, and I have seen plenty of others do exactly the same. A dedicated healer just isn’t all that necessary once you double down on damage or find more flexible healing elsewhere, like Shulk’s Light Heal. Sharla has been on my bench ever since, and I do feel bad about it, since none of this is really her fault.

In a recent development, for the longest time, I was shackled by what party composition makes sense for the story, and I still struggle with letting go of that sometimes. You will never catch me playing a Pokémon game without my starter, for example. In a similar vein, many of my Tales of Symphonia playthroughs simply ended up with Lloyd, Colette, Raine and Genis, because they are the ones who have known each other from the very beginning.

Eventually, I managed to get over myself. Since then, without fail, Genis has never been in my party again. I like the conversations between him and Lloyd, and I do believe that pairing a carefree character with a snarkier, more considerate one works out really well.

I just usually find him a bit grating. That is a harsh thing to say about a child who has been through as much as Genis has, and I’m aware of that every time I move him out of the party. It hasn’t stopped me yet.

According to recent reports, kongol always ends up benched. It’s common knowledge that Rose falls off quite aggressively on Disc 2, and again on Disc 4, which is unfortunate, but even she has seen more action in my playthroughs than he has. For the last surviving Giganto, that has to sting.

Sources indicate that my concern is simple: I don’t usually enjoy very slow characters, and Kongol is incredibly strong but painfully slow. To make him properly useful, you have to boost both his speed and his magic defence quite aggressively, and I would rather spend that effort on someone who doesn’t need it. He never stood much of a chance with me.

Luckily, The Legend of Dragoon isn’t a particularly hard game at the best of times, so you can beat it with any party you like. That takes some of the guilt away. Kongol saved Dart and his friends from a falling pillar before joining them, though, and I repaid him with the better part of four discs spent sitting around.

In a recent development, it pains me so much to say this, because I love dogs! In Dragon Age: Origins, however, Dog is close to useless compared to anyone else. Unless you install a mod, he takes up a full party slot, just like any other companion would, and he can’t carry a fight the way they can.

In a recent development, he does a semi-decent job in the first few levels, since Alistair and Sten aren’t great tanks at that stage, either. He then gets outscaled swiftly, as your warriors pick up their defensive talents and proper tank gear, and on Nightmare difficulty, that gap becomes very hard to ignore. Dog isn’t beefy enough to be a tank and doesn’t deal enough damage to make up for it, which leaves him without a clear role.

His Overwhelm ability is devastating against a single dangerous target, mages in particular, but that is about it. It’s a real shame, because his interactions with the other companions are often hilarious. Leaving him at camp means missing out on those, and it never gets any easier.

What is interesting, though, is that there exists a Extra Dog Slot mod that lets him tag along as a fifth party member, and it shows up on nearly every list of essential mods for the game. I am clearly not the only one with a guilty conscience.

Sources indicate that goofy has done nothing wrong, and I want that on record. My problem with the first Kingdom Hearts is that nearly every world offers a guest character who can take Donald’s or Goofy’s place, and I love how unique that makes each world feel. Somebody has to make room, and it was usually Goofy.

It has been revealed that recently, I felt really bad about that, and I wanted to make it right in my latest playthrough. Sadly, all it did was make me realise that the guest characters are a big part of the game’s charm for me. Fighting alongside Ariel or the Beast is simply too cool to pass up, and since they can’t leave their home worlds, it always feels like now or never.

Sources indicate that so Goofy might have to sit this one out a little longer. He will take it well, because he is Goofy. That only makes it worse.

Sources indicate that jean is the most painful example of wasted potential I can think of. His design is memorable, his personality is fun, and being the frog prince of SimaFort sets him apart from everyone else in Breath of Fire II. He believes that there are no bad people in the world, only bad hearts, and he claims all of it in a faux-French accent.

Mechanically, sadly, he has very little to offer. He joins slow and underwhelming, with good defence but incredibly low agility, and his stats never match the way he looks. His Holy fusion turns him into a tall, heroic-looking frog knight who can in theory become quite formidable, but it comes too late and with too many trade-offs to justify his slot over characters who have already proven themselves.

Jean isn’t unplayable. He is a “what could have been”: a character who looks like he should be iconic in battle, but never gets the chance to live up to it. If he had been a little more like Frog in Chrono Trigger, with some healing to offer, he might have been worthwhile well before the endgame.

Yangus is easily one of the most lovable characters in Dragon Quest VIII, and I still barely use him for long stretches of the game. He is the dedicated tank, and the job gradually overwhelms him: magic can lower his armour, most of his equipment reduces his evasion, and he is very slow. He has a respectable Strength base, but not much gets built on top of it.

In the 3DS version, which added Red and Morrie as party members, that makes him the obvious candidate for the sidelines once the new recruits join. He can become useful again in the late game, but that means building his Scythe tree from the ground up. That is a lot to ask for a character I have already replaced.

Sources indicate that it isn’t all doom and gloom, since he simply dips in the mid-game. Early on, 16 skill points in Humanity get you Nose for Treasure, which tells you how many chests are left in an area, and that is quite useful. I just wish that was enough to keep him in the party.

Sources indicate that nino joins with such a good story that you really want to use her and help her grow. Raised by the Black Fang, she is sent to assassinate Prince Zephiel in Battle Before Dawn, has a change of heart and ends up fleeing with Jaffar instead. By the time she joins you, it’s impossible not to root for her.

Unfortunately, she arrives as a Level 5 Mage very late in the game, when you are most likely fielding promoted units. Her growth rates are amongst the highest in the game, so she will catch up if you put the time in, but she’s a glass cannon until then, and there isn’t much game left. Unless you wrap your whole strategy around her, she gets benched immediately. This makes her a classic example of what Fire Emblem fans call the Est archetype: a unit that joins late and underlevelled, but with enormous potential.

Industry observers note that sometimes, it feels like her sole purpose is to stand between you and recruiting Jaffar, since he only joins if she talks to him and they both survive. This tiny mage is brimming with potential, and I have made use of it in some playthroughs. I’m just not always in the mood for that, so more often than not, she ends up on the bench.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion's Doctor Doom-Themed DLC Gives It The Post-Game Tail It Was Missing

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s.
  • I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on quickly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer.
  • In a recent development, seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s. While we still haven't heard any word of a upcoming brawler starring The Simpsons, Tribute did follow up its Turtle triumph with Marvel Cosmic Invasion, another throwback side-scrolling beat 'em up, this time starring Marvel's mightiest.

I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on quickly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer. Even after Cyclops and The Thing joined the roster as DLC in May, I still saw Cosmic Invasion as a game in the rearview. That changes this week, as The Siege of Castle Doom not only adds two additional playable characters (Invisible Woman and Doctor Doom), but also a mode that has the potential to bring me back for more runs for the foreseeable future.

In a recent development, seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands. Unfortunately, much in the way that it seems that he may try to fix the multiversal incursions in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, Victor Von Doom's solution in Marvel Cosmic Invasion – the Cosmic Inductor – would lead to untold death and destruction. In The Siege of Castle Doom, you select your team and fight your way through various floors of the stronghold belonging to the man who is perhaps Marvel's greatest villain. Your goal is to fight through the winding, randomized hallways of Castle Doomstadt, charging Reed Richards' Stabilizer and tactically bolstering your team along the way, before Doctor Doom can enact his proposal.

Industry observers note that as for the new playable characters, Doctor Doom is less agile, but his attacks pack a whallop, while Invisible Woman's force fields and speed make her the more versatile pick. I don't know that I see either of them replacing my mains from the base game, but I had fun experimenting with them throughout this mode. Regardless of which character you choose from the expanding roster, you still must traverse Castle Doomstadt before Doom achieves his objective.

Fighting through waves of enemies across differently themed and booby-trapped rooms, you encounter all manner of foes from the base game, as well as upcoming minion types from Doom. When you defeat enemies, they drop batteries that charge your Stabilizer, letting you even the odds and stop Doom. Conversely, each time an enemy hits your character, it charges Doom's Cosmic Inductor, inching him closer to victory and making his minions faster and stronger in the process. As you might expect, the rooms get harder the deeper you go, and while each player starts with two characters to swap between, if a character completely depletes their health, they're gone for good, making it even tougher. As such, you need to keep your eyes on each character's health and swap them out when it makes sense.

As you complete each room, you can choose which path to take to augment your characters with latest special abilities. True to the roguelite structure, as you complete rooms, you can also buff your characters' stats within the run. Certain rooms offer extra batteries to help your Stabilizer charge, while others offer new and upgraded equipment. There's also one that promises random events that can easily alter the trajectory of your run for better or worse. Though I often enjoyed boosting attack stats to make enemies less like damage sponges, I had to balance that against buffing their health to keep them alive and charging the Stabilizer to have a fighting chance.

Beyond the in-run upgrades and modifiers, you can also amp up the action run-over-run through upgrades in Reed's Lab, which add to the pool of modifiers you can select from at the start of each run. The expansion also adds newly introduced palettes for existing heroes, plus new music by composer Tee Lopes. While I've only done a few runs of The Siege of Castle Doom (each taking between 45 and 90 minutes, depending on how successful you are), I feel a revitalized sense of excitement for Marvel Cosmic Invasion. Tribute claims completionists can spend upwards of 15 hours in this new mode, which has me champing at the bit to dive back into what will likely be my primary way of interacting with Marvel Cosmic Invasion going forward.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion – The Siege of Castle Doom is available today on all platforms, and it is a strong addition to an already great game. You can read our review of the base version of Marvel Cosmic Invasion here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nioh 3 is one of the most anticipated games of 2026, and it’s easily among the biggest releases of February. We’re a few days away from the start of that month, however, but we don’t have to wait until then to actually play Team Ninja’s next major release.

The previously declared demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.

Unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game. This is pretty fresh for the series, which has typically launched first on PlayStation before coming to PC months later.

The Nioh 3 demo includes a decent portion of content from the beginning of the game. It’s enough to show off the core duality mechanic, letting you switch between the Samurai and Ninja styles at will. It also includes a preview of the game’s open field level design, which makes it sit somewhere between full open world and the more linear level design of past Nioh games.

Feedback from the previous beta has been implemented into the demo (and full release), so you may see some familiar faces, as well as areas you visited before - assuming you played that one.

Sources indicate that another major reason why you might want to grab the Nioh 3 demo is that your progress in it will carry over to the full version. This includes the character creator, too, meaning you can spend all day perfecting your character without having to worry about missing out on playing the actual game.

The demo even supports online multiplayer for up to three players, in case you come to Nioh for co-op. If you complete the available content, you’ll earn an in-game bonus in the full version. This is something Team Ninja has done with past Nioh titles, of course.

Industry observers note that this time, your reward is the Twin-Snake Helmet. Just make sure you complete the demo before February 15.

Nioh 3 is out February 6 on PC, and PlayStation 5.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Another day, another opportunity for some horsing around! I'm being literal here, to be clear, as a new upgrade for The Legend of Khiimori dropped yesterday. It's called The Mongolian Expanse, opening up the map a whole lot more and making a sweep of other additions to the game.

Previously, you might have looked out unto the snowy mountainscapes and the scorching deserts and thought "boy howdy am I glad I can't go there, those temperatures look like a nightmare to deal with!" Well, good news, as you now can head to those locales, each with "their own waystations, Yam nodes, named places, chests and bandit caches.".

Industry observers note that you don't want to wander there without some amount of prep, however, as the mountains are cold and difficult to climb, with wolves none too kind to humans like you. The desert, of course, is really hot, for both you and your horse. Both additions remind me of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and its use of extreme temperatures acting as a sort of challenge gate. Neat stuff!

According to recent reports, the buck doesn't stop there with this revision though. You'll find a whole host of newly introduced wildlife, ranging from wild boars, to gobi bears and camels. Of course, a horse game wouldn't be one without more horse, which there is! It's a new breed called the Marwari, a horse that is "built for endurance and especially resistant to heat, a strong partner for long, punishing Desert crossings." Beyond that, you'll also find more than 60 new horse skills, all findable across specific regions and for specific breeds.

It's a nice beefy patch with plenty more tweaks, additions and fixes on top of everything mentioned above. When it comes to the mountains and desert, you can also expect some big additions there, as this is only the first part of this update. You can read about everything else the update offers right here on Steam.

Final Fantasy Resonance producer Keisuke Nakashima has praised The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake as a great lesson in remakes.

Ignoring that it's from 1998, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the highest-rated game of 2026, and will likely hold on to that title until at least this Thursday when GTA 6 releases (maybe even longer).

In a recent development, but while a remake of one of the most beloved games ever is unsurprisingly a hit with players, other developers are coming out in force to praise the game too. Nier: Automata mastermind Yoko Taro has spoken about buying the remake because the original was such an influence on the Nier series. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, meanwhile, calls it a "terrific" achievement Nintendo should be proud of, even if some do call it a rival to GTA 6. And now, another developer behind a popular 2026 release has chimed in.

In a recent development, final Fantasy Resonance producer Keisuke Nakashima has now finished the Zelda remake and has taken to Twitter to share his thoughts (via machine translation). Nakashima calls the remake amazing, adding that it's a game he has played a ton since its original release on the N64. He then calls it a fantastic learning experience for remakes.

Square Enix's Final Fantasy Resonance – which broke the Steam record for the biggest player peak for a JRPG – has proved a hit with series fans. And while it's not a remake, it technically does remake some of the mobile title Final Fantasy: Brave Exvius. But, that game's status as a remake aside, it does look like Zelda is going to be a benchmark in remakes the same way 2002's Resident Evil and 2019's Resident Evil 2 have become.

Sources indicate that lord almighty, video games take a while to make, 'ey? Especially if you're just one person working on it by yourself. Such is the case with Faraway, out today, an arcade game that reminds me of the early days of PS3 indies "about a shooting star that creates constellations to stay alive," all made single-handedly by creator of cult-classic mobile game Eliss, Steph Thirion. Did I mention that Faraway took 16 years to make? Like I stated, game development is a lengthy process.

Recent findings suggest that looking at Faraway, and knowing how long it took to produce, it doesn't surprise me to come from a dev who managed to release a mobile game in the early days of the platform, long before free-to-play got its chokehold on the industry. It also really does feel like it should be sitting amongst the likes of PixelJunk, this thing should be something I'm desperate to play on my PS3 while I wait for my controller to charge.

It has been revealed that as mentioned, you are a shooting star, a "spark meant to shine and vanish in a blink." But still you persist, connecting to and wrapping yourself around starts to "harvest their energy," in turn lengthening your own life, and of course, in arcadey fashion, racking up a nice score. It looks like game design as poetry, everything you're looking at procedurally generated to bring freshness to every run. I can fully envision this as a "one more run" kind of arcade game, the best kind, especially in an age long past the need to shove in another of your hard earned coins.

In a recent development, faraway conceptually charms me because it taps into a style of game we don't get to see much of any more. What I'm saying is, I'm just a teensy bit sick of how many roguelikes there are, but that doesn't mean I don't want a game I can just hop in and out of at my own whims. The MOBA genre is competitive in every sense and Quantic Dream is trying to break into it with a Magic the Gathering-esque spin on the format. Players build a deck of cards before queuing into teams of 3, then face off as battling mages, summoning creatures, building fortifications and casting spells rather than choosing a Hero with unique abilities in the traditional MOBA style.

#17184. 8 Soulslikes With Insane Difficulty Spikes

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (843 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

8 Soulslikes With Insane Difficulty Spikes

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (843 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Soulslikes genre offers some of the greatest challenges in gaming.
  • However, there are times when a game takes it too far and includes a harsh difficulty spike that seemingly comes out of nowhere.
  • According to recent reports, while the games listed in this article are some of the best entries in the genre, they do have pacing concerns when it comes to difficulty.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Soulslikes genre offers some of the greatest challenges in gaming. With difficult bosses, enemies that demand patience, and many obstacles throughout a level, meeting success in any Soulslike can be incredibly rewarding.

However, there are times when a game takes it too far and includes a harsh difficulty spike that seemingly comes out of nowhere. This could sometimes lead to areas of the game feeling a bit unfair.

According to recent reports, while the games listed in this article are some of the best entries in the genre, they do have pacing concerns when it comes to difficulty. Here are eight Soulslikes with brutal difficulty spikes.

Sekiro is already a demanding game from the get-go, but its difficulty reaches a whole other level in the mid to late game. Enemies become more aggressive, minibosses hit harder, and all encounters will constantly remind players that they need to master the parry system to stand a chance.

Boss fights also become considerably more demanding, requiring players to learn lengthy attack patterns and maintain constant pressure rather than relying on dodging. Just when you thought you were getting good at the game, Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice raises the bar.

The expansion of Elden Ring, Shadow of the Erdtree, is known for its difficulty spike right from the start. As soon as you enter the Land of Shadow, you’ll realize enemies deal way more damage, and your character is much weaker overall.

It has been revealed that with the introduction of Scadutree Fragments, items that raise attack power and defense, players essentially have to start from scratch and engage with a upcoming progression system. In other words, even OP base-game builds get a wake-up call when starting the DLC.

Industry observers note that overall, Lies of P is generally on the easier side for a Soulslike. However, the game has brutal difficulty spikes in a handful of its bosses. For example, Laxasia the Complete, Simon Manus, and King of Puppets are ten times more challenging than anything else in the game.

Each of these bosses is a true test of reflexes and endurance, where even the smallest mistake can prove costly. What makes these encounters particularly jarring is the stark contrast in difficulty, as the areas leading up to them are relatively easy to breeze through.

There’s no denying that The First Berserker: Khazan is a very challenging game right from its first level. Still, despite it being a very tough experience through and through, it still features an insane difficulty spike in its second half that can sometimes feel pretty unfair.

Late-game bosses are some of the most demanding encounters the genre has to offer, featuring relentless combos that leave very little room for mistakes. Khazan’s combat is super satisfying, but players who haven’t mastered its mechanics will promptly discover just how unforgiving it can be.

While the 2023 version of Lords of the Fallen never reaches the difficulty heights of 2014’s, it’s definitely not an easy experience. The game reaches its peak in difficulty during Bramis Castle, an area filled with the hardest enemies in the entire game.

Bramis Castle has been heavily regarded as unfair by many players due to the absurd amount of elite enemies. It was so hard that there were multiple post-launch patches to make it feel more reasonable. Still, despite the patches to make it easier, Bramis Castle remains an insane difficulty spike.

Sources indicate that the original Hollow Knight was a fairly well-balanced experience from beginning to end, and while Silksong is a phenomenal game, it’s not as consistent as the original. For example, Bilewater increases the difficulty tenfold due to poisonous waters and brutal platforming.

Additionally, Act 3 of Silksong introduces an entirely latest set of challenges as the Void corrupts Pharloom, making enemies considerably more dangerous while changing areas and levels. Fortunately, Act 3 is completely optional, meaning players who aren’t interested in tackling this difficulty spike can simply ignore it.

Wuchang: Fallen Feathers features several notoriously sharp difficulty spikes, mainly in its boss fights. Wuchang has the tendency to make the player feel incredibly powerful while exploring a level and then completely ripping that feeling away during some of the main bosses.

According to recent reports, one of the earliest examples of this is the Commander Honglan boss fight, the first brick wall players will hit in a playthrough. All earlier bosses are a walk in the park compared to Commander Honglan, and everything that follows involves bosses that demand fast reflexes and perfect performance.

In a recent development, nioh 3's difficulty spikes can be particularly unforgiving, especially when players enter the Heian Period. This period involves some of the most challenging locations and bosses in the game, such as Ibaraki Doji, Kajiwara Kagetoki, and many more.

In a recent development, pretty much, once the player enters the Heian Period, the real Nioh 3 experience begins, and the rest of the adventure is a true test of skill. Bosses hit hard, are faster, and the importance of leveling equipment increases dramatically.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Not a Gen Z word in sight, phew.

It has been revealed that I was fully expecting a Gen Z word to win the Words With Friends Word of the Year. I’m technically part of that group myself, and I still couldn’t tell you what half of them mean, but that’s where I assumed things were heading. I was going to work a few of them into the opener to show willingness, but Whimsy isn’t really one for that, so that idea’s gone out the window.

The community vote ran over email and social media, with Whimsy beating runner-up Iconic in the final round. Iconic doesn’t really do anything for me. Whimsy seems like a good pick, though.

Recent findings suggest that in case you’re wondering, Whimsy is basically being playful or fanciful, whether that’s in how someone acts or how something looks. Zynga says it suits a year where people have been going looking for fun in unexpected places.

There’s a Word of the Year tile on the home screen from today, where you can check the pronunciation and definition, and Whimsy is playable in every mode, head-to-head matches and solo puzzles included. It’s six letters with a Y on the end, so it’s a decent way to get rid of high-value tiles too.

It has been revealed that slang did get a look-in last month, though. The dictionary revamp added more than 25,000 new words, modernised definitions and a first-ever way to report words, and slang like Cooked and Lore joined later in the month.

Words With Friends goes back to the Facebook games days, when Scrabble’s own mobile efforts hadn’t really taken off, and Wordle and the other cult-hit word puzzlers have been grabbing the attention for a while now. A vote like this is a nice way to keep people talking about it, I think.

If you want something else to play while you’re at it, there’s our list of the best puzzle games on iOS.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, open-world dress-up RPG, has delivered yet another major content drop in the form of Chromatic Beings Everbright. The latest update brings the game up to version 2.2, and introduces a new narrative chapter, and gameplay taking place around a festival narrative.

If you couldn’t guess already, the upcoming theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.

The major new story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm. This deceptively serene and blissful region hides a dark secret, however. Chromafaces, the mythical inhabitants of the realm, have to embody fixed identities that dictate how they live and work.

These are doled out through Character Tokens, which are used to assign roles to each individual. The story follows Nikki as she uncovers the script that runs the realm and the facade it props up. Nikki will help free Chromafaces and dispel the illusion.

In a recent development, the Wanxiang Realm is split into three areas. Cai Ye is your typical lantern-lit district, where festivals and fireworks happen. Kongming Gorge is almost the opposite of that; a quiet and cold place. Finally, Jiuhua Pavilion literally floats above the region, and it's home to neverending music and dance.

According to recent reports, the other massive addition in 2.2 are the two new 5-Star Resonance Outfits with some interesting gameplay implications. Where Wanxiang Weaves Life is inspired by wuxia aesthetics, and true to its inspirations, it lets Nikki shapeshift into different Spirit Personas - and automatically collect resources in her vicinity.

Chroma's Mortal Heart, on the other hand, allows Nikki to fly around the Wanxiang Realm, drawing on the power of the Celestial Deer. This outfit also uses Celestial Deer Vision to automatically ping and mark treasure chests around her.

You can also look forward to Nefarious Shadows, a upcoming Ability Outfit, which lets Nikki see through disguises, and reveals hidden paths in the world.

Sources indicate that as with every major update, of course, there are themed activities and limited-time events throughout. Hotpot House is a cooking minigame where you attempt to run the eponymous restaurant, whereas Flavor Frenzy is series of platforming challenges that tasks you with gathering ingredients. Fortune Mahjong is a little more straightforward, with support for solo and multiplayer play.

If you’re jumping back into the game soon, be sure to hit up our Infinity Nikki codes page for some freebies.

In a recent development, sometimes, you come across a game and instantly know it's for the sickos. Today that is Ablahshikar, a "turn-based salvage-survival CRPG adrift on the Candle Sea" where you rip out the organs of enemy warships to "rebuild your vessel into a doomed chimera," that is out now in early access. To be honest I could have just called it a CRPG and still labelled it as a game for sickos, yet everything that's going on here is obviously just doubling down on the sick factor.

It has been revealed that ablahshikar is a particular flavour of maximalism. Having not played it, it feels a bit impossible describe, I mean, just have a read of some of the game's Steam page: "Lo, destiny crooks a finger only to those whose eyes peer beyond þe next tempest. Take custody of a faltering war-barge that wanders the outer brine of Dastgerd. Thy wrists y-braced to a wan terminal of bone-whyte and tarnysshed latoun, þou steerest Ablahshikar by murke point-nettes and sputteryng tables." I don't know what any of that means! And I love it. Reminds me of Hylics in that the game's world is not translating itself for its audience; you take what you're given, and you figure it out yourself.

It has been revealed that judging from trailers and screenshots, there's a mix of activities to be getting on with. Occasionally you'll be piloting a strange, not alien, but definitely ancient ship of some kind in an arcadey sort of fashion. Then occasionally there's something that resembles Caves of Qud, i.e. some odd, 2D maybe dungeon crawling where your moves are dictated by individual keys on your keyboard. Then there's Disco Elysiumy cutscenes that feel like a video game designed in the year 1200 by someone from the year 2200, aesthetically anyway. As I said, it is a particular flavour of maximalism.

Sources indicate that truthfully, I do not know if I am sicko enough for Ablahshikar. Its mighty vision is terrifying, but I certainly am curious about it. Right now it's less than a fiver, and it'll only be in early access for roughly a couple of months where the price will then go up, so perhaps it's best to get in at the ground floor. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You may remember that a few months ago it came to light that a class action lawsuit was being filed against the three biggest RAM manufacturers on the planet, Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix. Obviously, the RAM crisis has been going on for the entirety of 2026, but a mix of individuals and stakeholder companies are accusing the massive three of working together to secure those high prices in a market they have almost total production control over.

In a recent development, well, it turns out that the makers of the best RAM for gaming filed a request to dismiss the case as nothing more than an attempt to "rerun" a very similar suit back in 2018. For those who don't know, this isn't the first time these companies have been accused (or found guilty) of price fixing. But the judge presiding over the case has assured it will press ahead.

Recent findings suggest that according to Tom's Hardware, Judge Noël Wise has dismissed the request for dismissal. When the massive three had argued they all have to watch one another "like hawks" to ensure reasonable pricing within the market, Judge Wise cleverly retorted, "Their contentions are more akin to hawks flying in formation — an activity that hawks ordinarily do not do.".

The lawsuit came about after a year of RAM shortages due to AI companies swallowing up the planet's supply of data, to the point where consumer and other tech markets have no supply to meet demand. Prices have soared, and Micron has even signed pricing guarantee deals with many of its clients, which ensure they'll be paying 2026-like costs for RAM until 2031 at least.

The lawsuit itself also comes after production of DDR4 RAM has been slowed down by all three RAM makers, forcing even more of a squeeze on the world's supply of DDR5 used by consumers, all sorts of tech, and AI companies building data centres.

Sources indicate that to make matters worse, the situation doesn't appear to be improving, even as AI bubble-bursting fears have seen massive hits to the share price of Google and Nvidia recently. Sam Altman recently met with Samsung to agree on renewed manufacturing deals for OpenAI's production. In 2025, the deal the two companies struck saw Samsung committing to supplying Altman's AI empire with roughly 40% of the world's entire supply of DRAM production.

Recent findings suggest that for those who don't know, 2018 saw a similar price-fixing suit against these companies that was ultimately dismissed due to a lack of evidence. However, in a case long before that, in 2005, Samsung and SK Hynix both pleaded guilty to a price-fixing conspiracy between 1998 and 2002. Samsung had to pay a $300 million fine, SK Hynix paid a $185 million fine, and Micron only avoided criminal prosecution by blowing the whistle on the other two.

This time around, according to Tom's Hardware, the massive three argued their recent behaviour doesn't indicate price-fixing and coordination; rather, three companies working similarly in a highly concentrated market "reacting to the same pressures" and making decisions that can maximise profit in a period of increased demand.

Nonetheless, the case will press on. Samsung, Micron, and SK Hynix have until December 7 to present their official rebuttals in a case management conference before the next steps are taken in early 2027.

Ever since I've been in love with video games and their technology. After graduating from Edinburgh Napier University with a degree in Journalism, I contributed to the Scottish Games Network and completed an Editorial Internship at Expert Reviews. Over the last decade, I’ve been managing my own YouTube channel about my love of games too. These days, I'm one of the resident hardware nerds at GamesRadar+, and I take the lead on our coverage of gaming PCs, VR, controllers, gaming chairs, and content creation gear. Now, I better stop myself here before I get talking about my favourite games like HUNT: Showdown, Dishonored, and Towerfall Ascension.

Remember fairytales? Of course you do; they comprise over half of all the inspiration for any given piece of media, and there's nothing wrong with that. There's a reason these stories keep getting told, and that's because of how accessible they are. Even with all the fantastical elements that occur in them, they're still pretty easy to follow and learn from. One such tale is that of Jack and the Beanstalk, which teaches you that it's totally okay to steal as long as you go through a botanically provided backdoor and the target happens to be a giant that would eat you if he could. This is the inspiration for Xalezar, who has given us Nymble 2 (giant presence notwithstanding).

Industry observers note that while you're never given a name, you fall into the role of a young and adventurous lad just looking to seek glory and fortune, supposedly. He discovers that he has the unique ability to interact with parts of the world by jumping over them. By using his skill, he has learned that certain patches of land will rapidly grow beanstalks leading to the upper levels of the world, which he will happily climb. It's your responsibility to manoeuvre his jumping effectively so that he can make it to the beanstalk safely.

Sources indicate that in order to keep climbing, the boy must keep leaping over fertile beanstalk soil. The challenge is that said patches of land are located in isolated areas that can invite all sorts of danger. Luckily, there are plenty of bountiful treasure chests to find in these lands that the boy can open with his jumping powers. Unfortunately, there are also hostile creatures that will be hunting the boy as he moves around the land. As long as he can get the jump on them, he'll live to make it to the beanstalk and get a few gold stars to boot.

According to recent reports, nymble 2 is the second instalment in the 2D puzzle-adventure series about a boy moving up in the world via jumping and magic plants. It's cute, quick, challenging, and a fun little way to keep your mind active while hanging out wherever you are. The more you climb, the more pieces come into play, and the more you'll have to direct your steps and your jumps. The boy has the power of youthful adventure, but sooner or later, he will have to grow up.

Nymble 2 is available to download and play from its itch.io page!

Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

In a recent development, aria is the other new arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

Industry observers note that beyond all the celebrations, this update also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a new outfit for Pan Yinhu.

The big event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Star Wars: Galactic Racer has proven to be one of the unexpected slam dunks of late 2026. In the little over a month since it was released, it has swiftly become exceptionally popular, both as another great game set in the Star Wars universe after Zero Organization, and a pretty great time of a racing game in general. It's even managed to inspired a healthy modding community. Heck, I don’t even like Star Wars, and I adore this game, having just rolled credits on the campaign the other day.

Recent findings suggest that one of the only major, consistent complaints towards Galactic Racer is its lack of local multiplayer features. The game does have online multiplayer, of course, but if you just wanted to run a few quick races with your buddies on the couch, you can’t do that, at least without everyone in the room having their own Steam Decks or something. This could be the single, crucial factor that definitively revives the spirit of games like Star Wars Episode I: Racer.

However, it seems the folks at Fuse Games have had their ears to the ground and heard the pleas of racing fans across the galaxy, because not only will Galactic Racer be getting that local multiplayer option soon, it’ll also get a little extra functionality on top.

Recent findings suggest that in a post to the official Star Wars: Galactic Racer X, formerly Twitter account, a representative of Fuse Games confirmed that the game will be receiving local split-screen functionality some time in early 2027. Rather than as an addition to the existing multiplayer structure, though, this functionality will be added in the form of an entirely newly introduced game mode.

“A dedicated team at @Fuse_Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to STAR WARS: Galactic Racer,” the post reads.

The game will be receiving local split-screen functionality some time in early 2027.

As the post explains, when you’re playing in free mode, not only will you be able to race freely with up to three friends in split-screen multiplayer, you’ll be able to freely select your vehicle, planet, race track, and character. The post also included a pre-release update build screenshot showing four players racing in split-screen, with the UI in each window adjusted to properly accommodate the radar, afterburner gauge, abilities, and Ramjet meter.

While the post didn’t specifically clarify this aspect, I’d assume players will be able to customize their abilities and vehicle components to some extent, given the ability menu’s presence.

According to recent reports, as someone who grew up in the N64 era, I can speak confidently to the power of split-screen racing games in making (and ruining) friendships. I can still remember the shouting matches I had with my sister over who got to be Yoshi in Mario Kart 64. If Galactic Racer can get full split-screen support, plus all the extra game-tweaking elements of Free Play, I think it could just become a contender as one of the best local multiplayer racing games of the current era.

It has been revealed that as I mentioned, many fans of this game have likened it to Star Wars Episode I: Racer, an N64 racing game focused on the Podracing elements from the film of the same name. While that game was fun enough on its own, it was the multiplayer that cemented it in peoples’ hearts and minds.

In a recent development, come to think of it, I hope Free Play lets you roll in Podracers as well, as that’d pretty much be the best possible way to capture that same magic. At the very least, I am confident that all multiplayer parties for Galactic Racer will have at least one argument over who gets to play as Biddy Blas.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It feels like every single week for the past few years has been the infinitely quotable 30 Rock quote on repeat. That feeling struck particularly last month when EA decided to shut down the iconic Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer BioWare. That obviously resulted in the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, of which a leaked trailer and some, now former, devs made sound pretty interesting. But hey! At least there's a documentary coming next year all about the studio that managed to capture the studio's last days! Yeah, I'm not so convinced by this upside either.

Recent findings suggest that as reported by Deadline, Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie will be helming a documentary about the beloved RPG studio for Canada's Super Channel. It's called, punnily enough, Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, and will apparently take a look at its origins in 1995 all the way up to its closure and a bit beyond, planned for release in 2027. Filming began two years ago, so clearly this was meant to be much more of a celebratory project than the funeral procession it's going to be.

Sources indicate that some substantial names from BioWare's history will be appearing in the doc, including its founders Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk and Augustine Yip, alongside the likes of longtime devs like Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Trent Oster, James Ohlen and Caroline Livingstone. You can also expect appearances from Jennifer Hale, Casey Hudson and, as if his sole goal is to haunt this industry everywhere, Geoff Keighley.

Recent findings suggest that in a statement, co-founders Muzyka and Zeschuk said, "When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and deeply moved. BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about the stories brought to life by the amazing people on our dev teams, and the fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We’re proud this film honors those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again.".

Obviously the documentary won't only be about the studio's closure, it sounds like a much bigger effort than that, so hopefully it will be a way to recognise how much of an influence BioWare has had on RPGs. It's just a ridiculous shame that it's something of a posthumous release. Continued solidarity with all those at BioWare.
