📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

It has been revealed that since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

Sources indicate that infinity Nikki is right now in one of the weirdest spots I have ever written about. Fans are proposing a boycott because Elon Musk's mom, Maye Musk, is the face and narrator of the game's latest revision.

The nepo baby has been embroiled in dozens of controversies, including an alleged Seig Hail salute, and his lack of gaming prowess has been highlighted time and time again.

By association, and holding some controversial views of her own, Maye Musk is an unpopular figure and a seemingly bizarre choice to front a marketing campaign for a video game update, but it's 2026, and we are here. The Chinese preview for Infinity Nikki's latest major update, Cicia, features Mrs. Musk in a gray suit, pointing at scenes from the game, describing the action. You can see the full 3-minute trailer below.

Industry observers note that the update teases a bunch of new features, but most notably, it includes the ability to drive a futuristic rocket-powered car. This reveal comes off the back of Elon's attempt to land a car driven up and flipped over a ramp, using thrusters to hit the ground safely.

The parallels with Tesla have fans worried, and using Maye Musk as the face of Infinity Nikki is enough to worry players, with early calls for a boycott.

"100% kneejerk reaction from the Chinese trailer, but..." a thread on the Infinity Nikki subreddit begins. "Latest car... Musk's mother... Semi-flying car... If Tesla is somehow involved in the design of the car (or worse, an in-game promotion), then I might have to let go." The post is tagged with the "girlcott/boycott" flair.

Industry observers note that the post has received dozens of comments in its first three hours, with an almost universal lamentation over Musk's inclusion. "I’m pretty bothered. Could have picked literally anyone else. Infold craves controversy. This game will never grow the way it should with these kind of decisions," said one from hadal_vt. "There's no way they would do this. There's no way they don't know how controversial Elon and Tesla are," added a second from ploobart.

In a recent development, I’m pretty bothered. Could have picked literally anyone else. Infold craves controversy.

While a minor boycott seems likely, its impact will be minimal. Maye Musk is reportedly a popular figure in China, where she has developed a large following and is seen as "a role model". Given that, last month, an estimated 82.5 percent of revenue came from China, Infinity Nikki will be fine.

It's not the first time the game has faced controversy, either. In 2025, a Stardew Valley crossover drew backlash, and excessive pricing in the game's Western launch left a sour taste in players' mouths.

Though it may seem like we just had a big life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

In a recent development, the game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Seed Sparkle Lab declared today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

The developer said to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access.

In a recent development, starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Sources indicate that speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese Latest Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

It has been revealed that on top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab says you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

Recent findings suggest that you can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

My favourite kind of game that's obviously going for the vibe of a particular era of gaming is one that doesn't look like it's trying to be any other game from noted era, moreso if someone told me it was a PS2 or a Dreamcast game everyone forgot about I'd believe you. CHRONO PUNK fits that vibe quite well, an action roguelite that looks like it's taking some cues from those aforementioned consoles, alongside the likes of Soul Eater, Jet Set Radio, Devil May Cry, and Spider-Man.

That is, obviously, a lot of things, but CHRONO PUNK on the surface appears to have its own identity at least. Your player character looks like an almost nightcore version of Sora Kingdom Hearts, with various roles and weapons to choose from; there's a sword and shield, pistols, shurikon, grimoire, and most Soul Eatery of all, a scythe. CHRONO PUNK's got vibes, too. The cities you do combat in are major and nondescript when it comes to details, but ripe for jetting about and Spider-Man-style swinging across the place. And besides, it looks like there's some hub areas ripped straight out of any stylised MMO from the 2000s.

I'm liking the look of the combat too. This'll obviously be one for the combo pilled out there, people who like to bounce back and forth between their enemies like a pinball. Slow paced, this is not. Sick, I hope this is. Pair all of that with some bouncy, wall running movement, and there's some real potential for a strong game here. Sounds like you'll be able to play it in co-op or solo too, which is a nice touch.

The story doesn't seem all that complicated, with some mega corporation manipulating time thereby controlling the city and the masses, leaving you to deal with the mess, but hey, I'm here for the vibes. As of right now, there's no release date attached to CHRONO PUNK, but you can wishlist it on Steam while you wait.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

This already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is at the moment number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

There are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

Critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Industry observers note that until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. Once you’re ready to get deeper, be sure to read up on how to play co-op with other players, and how to summon AI Acolytes to help you out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, members of the consortium led by the Saudi Arabian government's Public Investment Fund and some private equity suits which took over EA this year in a leveraged buyout worth $55 billion reportedly have a upcoming target in their sights. Unity, software manufacturer and makers of the game engine bearing the same name, have held talks with the consortium over a potential takeover, it's claimed.

Industry observers note that according to Reuters, a consortium including Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund and private equity firm Silver Lake Partners recently approached Unity about a deal that would value the company at around $25 billion. Unity are, it's claimed, presently working with an investment bank to evaluate their options following the chat, with no deal set in stone right now.

Silver Lake, Reuters note, are already among Unity's largest shareholders and invested up to $400 million in the engine builders in 2017. In fact, Silver Lake's managing director and CEO Egon Durban already has a seat on Unity's board of directors, so will probably have to butt out of any takeover talks.

Recent findings suggest that assuming the consortium would go the leveraged buyout route, loading Unity up with debt like the EA takeover did, it's hard to see any deal not resulting in similarly catastrophic consequences for those working at Unity. EA laid off a reported 400 people in an effort to cut costs after coming under the boot of the Saudi state and private equity, shutting BioWare and cancelling something Sims-related codenamed Project Lotus. BioWare's demise has since been reported to have largely come down to EA execs not wanting to fund both Star Wars Battlefront 3 and Mass Effect 5, with them opting to back only Battlefront 3.

Unity's recent financial results are looking strong, propped up by year-on-year growth in an AI-powered ad network dubbed Vector, so one would assume that bit of the business likely wouldn't be top of the list if any bloodletting was to end up happening.

Solidarity to any Unity workers who're now having to live under the shadow of this prospective takeover and the upheaval it could lead to if it goes ahead in a fashion which mirrors the EA deal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Recent findings suggest that since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Industry observers note that alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Industry observers note that sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

In a recent development, tensions between Taiwan and China are at an all-time high. While the Chinese government, led by Xi Jinping, believes Taiwan is part of China, Taiwan, its government, and its people view the country as an independent, sovereign state. Escalated military drills have taken place over the last year, as outside nations try to calm the issue.

Pikmin Bloom, the mobile Pokemon Go-like Pikmin title, has accidentally waded into the topic by labeling Taiwan as part of China in a recent update, leading to hurt feelings and boycott calls from people in the island nation.

First reported by Taiwanese outlet 4gamers, Pikmin Bloom, a game developed by Scopely, has referred to Taiwan as "Taiwan, China.".

An announcement for the game's 5th Anniversary event used the label in the Simplified Chinese version of the release. While 4gamers confirmed that the Traditional Chinese announcement reads "stores throughout Taiwan," the Simplified Chinese version remarked, "Japan and the Taiwan region of China.".

The glitch was spotted by Sherry Chou on Threads, who, in their post [translated by Google Translate], said:.

"Isn't this game completely unplayable in China? Taiwanese players are still the main source of income, so why are they still trying to curry favor with China? Are the official Pikmin game developers brainless or just used to kneeling? This game is making money off Taiwanese players. As a low-spending player, I can't stand it! If it's not fixed, I'm quitting." The post was dubbed "heartbreaking" by another Pikmin Bloom player.

As a low-spending player, I can't stand it! If it's not fixed, I'm quitting.

In a recent development, taiwan is presently Pikmin Bloom's biggest market. Spending from the country surged 902 percent in the first half of this year, as the walking/exploration game made $35.7 million, almost as much as it made in all of 2025. $18.5 million of the $35.7 million came from players in Taiwan, with the country taking a 52 percent market share in the first half of the year.

Recent findings suggest that japan still eclipses Taiwan in lifetime spend, contributing 49 percent of all-time revenue, but Taiwan is closing the gap. This growth in Taiwan has seen collaborations with local Taiwanese brands, including CoCo Fresh Tea & Juice and Family Mart.

It's the second time Pikmin has been involved in controversy in the last few days, with Pikmin 4's Dandori Academy Switch 2 Edition review-bombed and labeled a "scam.".

GTA 6 hacker who reportedly cost Rockstar $5 million pleads guilty to everything

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak of 2022 has now pleaded guilty after previously being indefinitely confined to a secure hospital.
  • It has been revealed that 21-year-old Arion Kurtaj had allegedly hacked Rockstar Games in a hotel room using an Amazon Fire Stick while on bail for previous crimes back in 2022.
  • In 2023, Kurtaj was deemed psychiatrically unfit to stand trial, and was later sentenced to indefinite life in a secure hospital, where he was set to remain unless deemed no longer a danger by doctors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak of 2022 has now pleaded guilty after previously being indefinitely confined to a secure hospital.

It has been revealed that 21-year-old Arion Kurtaj had allegedly hacked Rockstar Games in a hotel room using an Amazon Fire Stick while on bail for previous crimes back in 2022. This led to an enormous amount of GTA 6 footage hitting the web well before Rockstar had even properly revealed its upcoming title – the developer later said the incident cost $5 million and "thousands of hours of staff time" to recover from.

In 2023, Kurtaj was deemed psychiatrically unfit to stand trial, and was later sentenced to indefinite life in a secure hospital, where he was set to remain unless deemed no longer a danger by doctors. A mental health assessment had previously determined that he "continued to express the intent to return to cybercrime as soon as possible. He is highly motivated.".

Sources indicate that earlier this year, however, it was reported that Kurtaj had been released from the secure hospital where he was being held as he awaited a criminal trial, and that's what's happening now. The BBC reports that today at Woolwich Crown Court, Kurtaj pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar, in addition to other hacks he carried out with cybercrime group Lapsus$. He reportedly revealed no emotion. This comes just days before the actual release of GTA 6 on November 19.

During his time in prison, Kurtaj was also caught using a phone, according to the BBC. As well as reportedly taunting the police with a text message, he apparently posted updates to Snapchat, with the outlet sharing a selfie captioned: "Phone about to be seizedi think will get another soon inshallah".

Today, Kurtaj also pleaded guilty to physically assaulting workers while he was in custody – the BBC notes that this included biting people. The hacker hasn't been sentenced yet.

GTA 6 won't make kids violent, UK Conservative Party leader thinks: "Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter – I didn't hit anybody after playing those.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I have been a big fan of Casetify for my entire adult life.
  • Recent findings suggest that the KOJIMA PRODUCTIONS x CASETiFY collection does have a bunch of different designs, including little plushies!
  • This phone case is sleek - black and grey, with slight designs on it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I have been a big fan of Casetify for my entire adult life. I do feel that their cases are just fantastic, and when they confirmed their collab with Death Stranding 2, the action-adventure game by the legendary Kojima Productions, I was excited to see their designs!

Recent findings suggest that the KOJIMA PRODUCTIONS x CASETiFY collection does have a bunch of different designs, including little plushies! It's quite fun to see these different takes on the video game. I had a look at the DS2 - DHC Magellan Set, which has three different aspects to the set itself.

The first aspect is the phone case. This phone case is sleek - black and grey, with slight designs on it. It's not in-your-face Death Stranding 2, but it's one of those if you know and are a fan, you know. I have had several compliments for this case, especially at gaming events, which is always nice. There is a small double-hole bit on one side, perfect for phone charms if that's your thing. The case is a MagSafe case, so you can use the magnet on the back of it to attach any other MagSafe products to it. Casetify cases are high-impact, so there is no need to worry about dropping your phone, and I feel that my phone has always lasted in these.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of the MagSafe case, this set came with the Snappy Grip Stand MagSafe Compatible backing, which easily snaps into place using the magnet. I like the pop of colour this adds, though it does cover some of the design on the back of the case. Unlike PopSockets, which can be quite bulky, it sort of folds flat. Popping it up and placing my fingers into it feels very comfortable to hold. I did find that it's not really for constant use (or it might have been my batch), as when it was in my pocket it got a little warm and felt sticky on the edges from the glue holding it together.

The third item within the DS2 - DHV Magellan Set is the AirPods Pro 3 Impact Case, which is a two-part protective case which fits well over the top of your AirPods. The clip itself is very durable, with the Casetify logo on it, and doesn't feel like it would fall apart or anything. It's simple, but well designed.

I have always been a fan of Casetify and very much like these collabs! These make great gifts for gamers and are also extremely functional as well.

Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a latest world, and a Fortnite collaboration

📅 06 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (871 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • HoYoverse just wrapped up a major Honkai: Star Rail Special Program.
  • The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason.
  • Sources indicate that planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a major Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the substantial new world headlining Version 4.0.

Sources indicate that planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

Recent findings suggest that the squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

According to recent reports, the imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

Recent findings suggest that the Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

According to recent reports, much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

In a recent development, version 4.0 introduces two newly introduced 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

It has been revealed that general Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

It has been revealed that her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other fresh arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

In a recent development, when you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the newly introduced outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

Sources indicate that if you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be confirmed at a later date.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Halloween might be over, but Pokémon Go is giving the chance to unleash horrors upon its world, as the worst clothing item ever produced by human hands is coming to the game, and fans can acquire it for free.

Pokémon Go has had multiple controversies regarding player avatars; back when Niantic was running the game, there was a massive downgrade in character quality. Suddenly, characters lacked curves, and everyone became a generic outline, with detail plummeting across the board.

It has been revealed that the backlash against the bad Pokémon Go avatars has diminished over time, but that hasn’t stopped the game from receiving some terrible outfits. The next one involves a type of shoe that is an abomination upon humanity, and one set of them is available in Pokémon Go for free.

In a recent development, crocs are the worst shoes ever made, being marginally better than leather boots filled with thumb tacks worn by masochists. However, people buy them, and this has led to geek crossovers such as Yu-Gi-Oh! Crocs, and recently, Pokémon.

Industry observers note that the official Pokémon Go website has declared that the Crocs crossover has arrived in the game and will run until December 31, 2027, giving players ample time to acquire them. One of the sets is completely free, being the Pokémon Pikachu Classic Clog item, which can be claimed by using the code POKÉMONGOxCROCSxELECTRIFYING in the game.

Recent findings suggest that two other sets of Pokémon Go Crocs can be claimed: Pokémon Gengar Classic Clog and Pokémon Jigglypuff Classic Clog. These can only be claimed by the sickos who purchased them in real life, and they’ll be sent a free code to download them.

The player avatar in Pokémon Go is pretty small, and they don’t appear on the screen all that much, as the game is mostly focused on catching Pokémon and battles. That being said, players care about how their in-game avatar looks, often going for attractive, cool, or downright weird models to stand out from the crowd. This is why the in-game cosmetics industry is so profitable.

Then again, there’s a certain kind of fan that loves the items everyone hates. Indeed, some people wear Crocs for this exact reason, imagining themselves as some kind of Cyberpunk-era James Dean rebel, wearing their awful plastic shoes with holes in them, rather than the sad, soulless wretches they truly are.

Sources indicate that perhaps the idea behind this crossover is to attract the Pokémon Go whales who buy everything associated with the game. They’ll have to buy some Gengar and Jigglypuff Crocs to stay in the loop and ensure they have every avatar item at their fingertips. Whether such fans remain after years of lackluster Pokémon Go updates remains to be seen.

Recent findings suggest that in the end, it’s hard to be mad at a company giving away goodies for free. Maybe there’s a fan out there who is still stuck with the basic Pokémon Go avatar shoes and wants something a bit nicer for their little character to strut around the overworld in. Maybe that’s the point of all this, as walking around in Crocs for long enough can make any player reach for their wallet and buy some premium cosmetics.

"It's a brave new world": GTA 6's PC port will release sooner than you think to avoid losing money to AI rip-offs, indicates former Rockstar tech director

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1047 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6's PC release may come sooner than anticipated, according to former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij, because Rockstar and publishers Take-Two will be concerned about losing money to unofficial generative AI clones of the PS5 version, once it rolls out on 19th November.
  • Speaking to me during a wide-ranging chatathon, Vermeij reflected on the early days of Grand Theft Auto development at Rockstar North in the 90s, and how the Noel-and-Liam-Gallagher-esque relationship between PC and console gaming has evolved.
  • Sources indicate that "I didn't work on GTA 1 and 2, but I worked for the manufacturer at the time, and I was actually right next to the GTA 1 team, so I was able to follow it," he said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6's PC release may come sooner than anticipated, according to former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij, because Rockstar and publishers Take-Two will be concerned about losing money to unofficial generative AI clones of the PS5 version, once it rolls out on 19th November. In general, Vermeij thinks that how to avoid having your games duplicated by chatbot herders is "the massive question" right now for devs and publishers, particularly those who don't have the means to enforce their intellectual property dominions as vehemently as Take-Two do for Grand Theft Auto.

Speaking to me during a wide-ranging chatathon, Vermeij reflected on the early days of Grand Theft Auto development at Rockstar North in the 90s, and how the Noel-and-Liam-Gallagher-esque relationship between PC and console gaming has evolved. He shared a sweary anecdote about the tech giant's difficulties getting the original GTA 1 to look the business on Sony's PlayStation.

Sources indicate that "I didn't work on GTA 1 and 2, but I worked for the manufacturer at the time, and I was actually right next to the GTA 1 team, so I was able to follow it," he said. "So they worked on PC and then an external company in Dundee did the PlayStation version. Which was really weird, because like, PCs were so much more powerful - still the case, but in those days, it was even more so.

"And I remember, at the time, the GTA team was definitely the most rowdy of all of the teams," Vermeij continued. "And there was one particular day where they sent the PC build away, and then it came back from the PlayStation people, and they had cut down all the textures from 256 colours to 16 colours, and my god, the artist was just going around and swearing - 'what the fuck did they do to our textures, I can't believe it, we can't release this shite'. So it always has been that sort of awkward relationship between PC and the console. So in those days, it was like PC first and then console second, even though that didn't really make much sense for the sales, because the PlayStation versions sold way better.".

When it came time to develop GTA 3, Rockstar "flipped that around", Vermeij went on, creating the console versions first. "Clearly the PC market has sort of grown, caught up with the console market, but there's still that same mindset," he said. Most publishers prefer to release all versions at once, Vermeij added, "because then there's only one marketing campaign they have to pay for." GTA lives by its own rules, however. "I guess it's less of an argument for them because the game is just so big, so they just kind of always left it that way. And for developers, it's way easier to just do one version at a time. So, you know, that makes sense.".

The arrival of generative AI threatens to throw all this to the winds. Tools such as Reverse Engineer Anything allow for speedy unofficial ports or "slopcomps" of console games on PC, despite warnings from seasoned recomp developers that using genAI for this purpose wrecks the community aspect of unofficial porting, and results in illegible "bruteforce" code rather than preserving some understanding of how the original game was made.

"It really has changed the world," Vermeij observed, "and I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be won't be as good as their effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together. Obviously, I don't really know what they're thinking.".

GTA 6 is, according to Rockstar and Take-Two at least, an enormously fiddly production, costing hundreds of millions of dollars over eight years in development. Nonetheless, Vermeij thinks current genAI tools are "probably" capable of pulling off a port. "It will take a long time. It actually, physically takes hours and hours and hours to do these things. And it will take a bunch of tokens and everything, so it would probably cost like, tens of thousands of dollars in tokens. But like, you know, if it's GTA, I think people are gonna try it.".

Recent findings suggest that there are already signs that genAI PC port goldrushers are ready to pounce on GTA 6. Just today, Ars Technica reported on efforts to yassify the game's PS5 trailer footage by piping it through a stronker PC graphics card and using Nvidia's DLSS 5 to apply extra layers of gloss.

In a recent development, vermeij himself left Rockstar way back in 2009 and is now an indie developer. His current early access project is Plentiful, a hexagonal god sim with an emphasis on water physics. It uses "AI-assisted machine translation for localization", but not for "gameplay content, art, or audio". Vermeij is, in general, interested in generative AI despite the surging tide of slopcomp ports. Smaller indie developers are, of course, more vulnerable to the financial fallout from having their work unofficially cloned by generative AI, but Vermeij thinks it's an existential worry for megacorps like Take-Two as well.

"I don't really see how you could protect against that, to be honest," he told me in closing. "I don't see it. But a major manufacturer like Take-Two, they would be able to get the lawyers on the case, and maybe, like, you remarked, for a big game, maybe the AI doesn't really do a particularly good job. But yeah, I mean, it's a brave new world. What was the case before, is that there's so much effort in developing the game, that it is not possible to rip it off, and that's completely changed now. So, yeah, we're going to have to see in the next couple of years, how that's going to pan out.".

The latest rumour-mongering places GTA 6's PC release sometime in early 2027. In other news, Rockstar staff are soon to formally vote on whether to apply for union recognition. If the organisers carry the day, the resulting union could encompass nearly all the manufacturer's UK staff below management level.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mojang hosted a surprise Minecraft Dungeons II broadcast at TwitchCon San Diego this year, and alongside this, it's announced the first paid DLC will be arriving very soon.

Industry observers note that the Humblers Awaken will launch on 1st December 2026 and brings a fresh adventure to the action-RPG with new quests, unexplored environments, colourful cosmetics and an expanded arsenal of gear. Here's a bit more about what you can expect:.

According to recent reports, "The Sift is in danger once more, and the humblers – an ancient threat that has slumbered for ages – are beginning to wake up. Turns out they are not particularly happy about it, and if left unchecked, they will spread across the dimension, or worse – stir a much more dangerous foe. It falls on you and your trusty allies to venture into the dimension’s deeper reaches and investigate this strange unrest.

"The journey will take you through the sprawling fungal sporefields and winding underground burrows, with new quests shedding light on the mystery behind the humblers’ rude awakening.".

This DLC will also add "three new artifacts that provide active abilities" and "four new talismans offering passive bonuses". Additionally, there's some cool new equipment including The Pearl skin, the Baby Nuzzle pet and Nacreous cape.

In a recent development, alongside this DLC will be a bonus free patch - this will add latest challenges, more weapons and armour to Minecraft II. It will also reunite heroes from the original Minecraft Dungeons (Hal, Hex, Adrienne and Valorie) as player skins. There'll also be the new trial dungeons, where you can earn powerful gear:.

"Take on the newly introduced trial dungeons to earn powerful gear. Available through Brave Haven, trial dungeons offer daily and weekly challenges that feature a combination of rule-bending modifiers and increased difficulty. Enormous spiders, constant TNT explosions, and soul projectiles are just some of the modifiers you will encounter in these dungeons!".

Last but not least, it's been confirmed the DLC 'Illusions of Grandeur' will launch at some point in Spring 2027.

Will you be checking out the first DLC for Minecraft Dungeons II? Have you played the second game yet? Let us know in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that heartopia has officially shared initial details about its first-ever collaboration event. The game, which debuted a month ago to great success on mobile, as well as Steam on PC, has already been a staple among fans of Animal Crossing and The Sims.

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

In a recent development, the Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

The first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

Industry observers note that the ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

It has been revealed that the more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

Badge Pull Tokens are your significant reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

In a recent development, heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

Sources indicate that we also recently updated our guides on how to catch Frostspore fish - and if you’re into cooking, how to obtain every recipe and variant. If you haven’t already, definitely see if you missed any of these Heartopia codes, too.

Slay the Spire 2's new character The Fool is the most going-to-be-nerfed slayer since The Watcher

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that slay the Spire 2's November 12 revision saw the biggest-ever patch hit the denizens of the titular spire the same way a meteor hit the Earth as the dinosaurs watched.
  • In a recent development, "We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch," Mega Crit remarked in the beta patch notes.
  • I've reached Ascension 9 with The Fool so far, and here's my favorite strategy: kill everything in one hit or gain 10 billion block a turn until you can do that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that slay the Spire 2's November 12 revision saw the biggest-ever patch hit the denizens of the titular spire the same way a meteor hit the Earth as the dinosaurs watched. The game's first newly introduced character, The Fool, is balanced like a barbell with six plates on one end and two on the other – by far the most overpowered class since The Watcher disrupted the original Slay the Spire.

In a recent development, "We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch," Mega Crit remarked in the beta patch notes. "Even more importantly, be sure to have fun figuring out all the strategies and story of this gently bard. It would be foolish not to!".

I've reached Ascension 9 with The Fool so far, and here's my favorite strategy: kill everything in one hit or gain 10 billion block a turn until you can do that. I find that this usually works.

Industry observers note that your average turn with The Fool feels like the kind of Regent high-roll you tell all your Discord friends about. The class has three main mechanics: shooting and dislodging arrow-type attacks that deal heavy damage, generating three temporary melodies (wah, cho, and ki) with myriad effects and conditional bonuses, and creating curse-like cards called sadness (which clog your hand) to convert them into joy (which give you one extra card and energy when played).

Recent findings suggest that drafting too many arrow cards is a recipe for disaster, as you can only play shots when you have arrows to spare (you only have one to start) and you can only dislodge arrows that are presently impaled in enemies. There is no true 'arrow deck,' only a package of overpowered arrow cards like the multi-shot nonsense that will see you deal 400 damage for one energy without breaking a sweat. Get one good multi-hit shot and one decent source of Aim (vigor that only buffs arrow attacks) and you'll delete anything soon enough.

Sadness is similarly appetizer-sided but seems weaker so far. I've only found a few sadness cards that I actually like – Vitriol applies weaken, Ennui draws more cards but creates sadness, and Brighten Up gives you three joy at the cost of two sadness – and the pool here feels pitifully small and rare-dependent. Yet The Fool remains comically overpowered.

Melodies are the core of The Fool, and they are not OK. Ki Rest gives you five (or, upgraded, six) mana next turn and can retain your hand with a cho melody in play. Wah Symphony scales off the melody cards in your deck and can easily deal 100 AoE damage for two energy. Wah Cho Ki does everything you want – draw, block, damage – and instantly fills your melody repertoire for bonus synergies. Even the common cho cards are among the best cheap blocks in the game, if only for their added keyword value.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

It has been revealed that it's telling that I already know this many melody cards off the top of my head. Even without a rare-grade bomb like Wah Symphony, you can just hit a critical mass of melodies and become unstoppable, with strong powers giving you extra block from cho cards and extra draw from any melody. My most dominant runs are generally defined by how many Ki Rests I hit anyway.

Also: The Fool's form card, Mythic Form, is handily the strongest of the six, generating unique tarot cards with monstrous effects.

The Fool has some of the clunkiest individual cards in Slay the Spire 2, but their overall power level is obscene – handily the strongest version of a class the game has ever dealt with. The whole Slay the Spire community is presently a storm of posts and videos sarcastically arguing that "The Fool is fine, actually" while A10 bosses are carbonized in the background.

The first balance pass from Mega Crit, whenever it comes, is sure to be seismic. Some melody cards deserve a humbling, but I also hope to see arrows become more consistent and sadness become more relevant. The archer-bard flavor of the class is fantastic, but a little bard-heavy at the moment.

Slay the Spire 2 devs declare the "perfect card," and of course it's one I thought was bad.

Industry observers note that austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible.

Why's this happening now? Well, an EA producer stumbled across a cupboard full of old tapes, film reels and CDs.

It has been revealed that according to an interview with The Game Business, the discovery of this old gubbins was a consequence of EA senior producer Jim Vessella needing somewhere upcoming to stick a bunch of Betacam tapes used to help make the Command & Conquer Remastered Collection. "One of the facilities people was like, 'I think there’s a room in the other building that has a couple of items like that'," Vessella recalled. "He took me over there, opened it up and it was like Indiana Jones… just, whoa. Knowing what I’d discovered with the Command & Conquer tapes, I really felt like we had to find out what was on all these tapes.".

The producer was able to convince EA's bosses that this stuff was worth the work needed to stick it back on storefronts, and lo, an EA blog post gushing about their vault's door having slid aside to reveal this pile of retro games. The collection includes restored versions of the following games, all with "robust quality-of-life updates and higher resolution Full-Motion Videos (FMV) from the Master tapes":.

Meanwhile, the rest of the lineup is filled out by "faithful ports" of the following:.

On Steam, all of these are currently on sale for less than a fiver each, with the prices of the most expensive ones set to rise to just under £10 when the introductory offer expires on November 19th.

It's good news in preservation terms, though I'm not sure it totally washes away the bad vibes of EA's Saudi and private equity owners reportedly looking to take over Unity.

It is also, quite visibly, the most popular Nioh release ever on PC, and it was impressive watching more and more players jump into the game over the weekend and push the numbers higher.

In a recent development, nioh 3 came out swinging, breaking the series’ Steam concurrent player record immediately after lanch, with 42,822. Anyone keeping up with how well the game has been received, and how much it’s been anticipated by series fans and Soulslike players, would’ve told you that it was only the beginning.

Late on Friday, and several times on Saturday, the game continued achieving new records, setting new peak concurrent levels every couple of hours. It happened again on Sunday, when the game finally settled on its current 88,045 peak concurrent (via SteamDB).

Industry observers note that that’s an incredibly healthy player base, but more than that, it’s more than double the previous record holder, Nioh 2, which peaked at 41,325 concurrent players in 2021. Steam players appear to be very happy with the game, too, with over 1,560 reviews and an overall Very Positive rating.

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

According to recent reports, since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

According to recent reports, sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

We've only just had the release of the Pokemon Trading Card Game's most recent expansion, Delta Reign, but it seems like attention is already moving on from that set to the next, Flowing Fists.

Although Flowing Fists doesn't launch until February next year, some people on social media have begun getting their hands on products early, giving us our first look at some of the cards in the set, including a stunning Blastoise Illustration Rare.

In a recent development, the upcoming Flowing Fists set will pull cards from the Japanese-language expansion, Aura Seeker. As the name might suggest, the expansion will be centered around Mega Lucario Z, which was first introduced in Pokemon Legends: Z-A last year. We've had early glimpses of the Japanese Mega Lucario Z ex and Mega Garchomp ex Special Illustration Rares, and now the English versions, along with a handful of other unrevealed cards, have come to light.

It's unclear how, but some people have managed to get their hands on a bunch of single Flowing Fists blisters and are pulling what will undoubtedly be the set's most desirable cards.

As is so often the case, the images look like they've been taken on a potato, but the quality of the cards shown mean the set is going to be an exciting one.

In a recent development, the Mega Garchomp Z Special Illustration Rare features the Pokemon rocketing toward the camera, its two blades ready to attack. It can be seen below:.

The Mega Lucario Special Illustration Rare was also pulled early, and features the new form of the Pokemon looking rather majestic. It's ability, Aura Seeker, matches the Japanese set's name.

The star of the show, though, is the Blastoise Illustration Rare. While it may have been "demoted" from Special Illustration Rare status, with the last one it received coming in the 151 set, this card is spectacular. It features one of the coolest depictions of the Pokemon standing in a rocky cavern, surrounded by water. I may be a little bit of a Gen 1 simp, but it's a great card.

Should more photos emerge throughout the day, we'll update this article, but I have a feeling Flowing Fists will be better than any standard set the Pokemon Trading Card Game received this year.

When you reach Rank 1 for any new Memory from the banner, you’ll earn a Memory-themed outfit with a special colour that matches your chosen love interest.

Sources indicate that illusio returns as part of the fresh event, too, letting you customise the look of Kindled Moments across all five new Memories. Things you can customise include selecting the outfits and accessories for each love interest, so you can recreate Kindled Moments in your own style. As always, Kindled Moments will go back to their default look after the event ends.

There’s a new mini-game to play, too, available only during the event. It’s called Courteous Fare, a frantic but familiar restaurant management simulation that allows you to unlock a variety of rewards.

Airframe Ultra's PS1 cyberpunk city is an amazing tribute to G-Police and WipEout, and I wish you people would slow down to appreciate it

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (744 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that I do not wish to "rule the streets" of Megacity West, dear creators of Airframe Ultra.
  • In a recent development, those eroded pastel chevrons.
  • Industry observers note that despite my best efforts, Airframe Ultra is a battle racer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I do not wish to "rule the streets" of Megacity West, dear creators of Airframe Ultra. I wish to be ravished by them, rubbing my face against the rusty corrugated metal of the shipping containers, and savouring the acid blue waters of the bay. I do not want to "become the one thing with freedom in a city of billions: A racer." I want to become the other thing with freedom in a city of billions: a person who slowly drives or – whisper it - walks around just looking at stuff, because gadzooks, this is one of the prettiest PS1 cyberpunk burgs I've laid eyes on.

In a recent development, those eroded pastel chevrons. Those seductively wobbling vertices. That electric reef of a downtown backdrop, murderously luring your gaze from the on-coming trucks. That layer of invigorating crackle over everything. Every moment or so, I dismount from my hoverbike to inspect some concrete ruin I could swear I last saw in G-Police, or ponder the resemblance between a subway tunnel and WipEout 2097's Gare d'Europa. Then, somebody waps me in the skull with a stop sign at 300 kilometres an hour. But I was already stopped, frantic stranger! Your brutal poetic ironies are wasted on me.

Industry observers note that despite my best efforts, Airframe Ultra is a battle racer. It's co-developed by Videocult, the people behind Rain World – a game it looks nothing like, but is comparable to in the sense that there is an ocean of industrial refuse to navigate, and you will very often die. Each battle race is broken into sprints around a branching course that has been smashed together by the forces of urban decay. You will corkscrew down storm drains and barge through old abandoned clifftop mansions under a scarlet sun, zip along deadly flyovers and thread the barely legible layouts of high density slums.

Your hoverbike handles like a bronco full of helium, and that's before you start wanging it off the gloriously marbled, low-poly rubbish heaps that stud the city, shunting the game's camera through surfaces and exposing the map's underside in what the absolute squares amongst my readers will doubtless deem "an inelegance", but which true turbojunkeys will appreciate for its makeshift exuberance.

According to recent reports, you've got a boost button which generally gets you exploded – and all that's before you get to the time-limited battle arenas that bookend each sprint. Here, players attempt to slaughter each other as much as possible, spending collectible cash on floating weapon pick-ups that range from bent pipes to Gatling guns and EMP grenades. Then it's off for another sprint. The first player to earn 10 points and place first in a subsequent sprint wins the match. I have not won many matches. My primary goal right now in Airframe Ultra is persuading everybody to stop and swap some emotes, while I coo over an amazing piece of graffiti I've found.

Industry observers note that my efforts to make Airframe Ultra a walking sim aren't just about scenery. The game is surprisingly engrossing on foot, with some woozy tank controls that make me think of the experimental days before every third-person control scheme became a variation on Assassin's Creed, Uncharted or Gears of War. You have to hammer a button to run, for instance, and you'll wind yourself fast. You can also perform punches and kicks in four directions, with grander attacks to discover by smooshing together inputs. You'd best believe I burst into tears when I realised what this reminded me of: it's Bungie's Oni! The game with the finest martial arts system ever coded! There are more obvious influences, like Road Rash, but in these grim days of endless parrying, I'll take all the Konoko callbacks I can get.

Ahhhhh. But if only this had a proper single player mode. Online and local splitscreen with drop-in bot support are all you get. I wouldn't say Airframe is the most balanced deathracer, either. In my experience, and do bear in mind I mostly try to avoid the racing component, victory typically goes to whoever lands a fat cash reserve and grabs an AK47. That mild shambolicness is arguably part of the charm, in that it supplies incentive to stop and drink in the atmosphere. These streets are substantial and broken and beautiful enough for all of us, friends. Let us rule them together. Read more on Steam.

Capcom has revealed the winner of the Mega Man: Dual Override Robot Master design contest, with the winning character set to officially appear as an in-game boss.

In a video hosted by director Shinya Ikuta and producer Hiroyuki Minamitani, the pair showcased the six finalists before revealing that the winner is... Cleanser Man!

According to recent reports, submitted by artist 'iregyuradabii', Cleanser Man was chosen as the winner "after many discussions and careful consideration", with Ikuta-san stating that the selection process was "incredibly difficult for the entire team". The remaining finalists will have their names appear in the in-game credits.

Here's an message from the dev team:.

All of the 6 finalists had some really great and unique ideas, and the entire dev team has been very impressed and amazed at the amount of creativity on display.

It wasn't easy picking a winner, but we ended up deciding on Cleanser Man due to his whimsical motif and unique color pattern.

The lid part on the detergent has a very Mega Man-esque design to it, and we like that the detergent itself is very colorful as well.

You have to be careful not to introduce too many elements to prevent the design from becoming too cluttered, so we like that the artist kept things relatively simple.

But there's still enough detail to it to give it that genuine Mega Man feel.

Once again, thank you to everyone who joined in the contest.

We really appreciate the time and effort everyone put into this.

And here's a look at Cleanser Man. Be sure to check out the video above to see it in action:.

Mega Man: Dual Override is scheduled to release on Switch and Switch 2 in Spring 2027. So far, five Robot Masters have been confirmed, including Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, Cook Man, and the prize-winning Cleanser Man. There are still three left to reveal, so we'll keep a close eye on future announcements.

In a recent development, what do you make of the Robot Master design contest winner? Do you think Capcom chose the right design? Let us know with a comment.

The SteelSeries Rival Pro offers some unique tools, but with a price that'll put some buyers off

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1930 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the SteelSeries Rival Pro rides or dies on its two unique features: the Ultra-Wideband connectivity, and its "unlimited" battery life through a fast-swap mechanism.
  • Why you can trust GamesRadar+ Our experts review games, movies and tech over countless hours, so you can choose the best for you.
  • You may know SteelSeries as making many of the best gaming headsets, but it’s returning its attention to another kind of gadget with the Rival Pro (and three siblings: the Sensei Pro, and a Mini equivalent of each).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the SteelSeries Rival Pro rides or dies on its two unique features: the Ultra-Wideband connectivity, and its "unlimited" battery life through a fast-swap mechanism. These work wonderfully, and go some way to justifying the premium price, though not everyone will find UWB a useful addition. Plus, the design lacks a few refinements, feeling a little cheap in the hand, and depending on your desk set-up the base station may be more than your set-up can take.

UWB is a novel and useful addition.

Base station may not fit in some set-ups.

Why you can trust GamesRadar+ Our experts review games, movies and tech over countless hours, so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about our reviews policy.

You may know SteelSeries as making many of the best gaming headsets, but it’s returning its attention to another kind of gadget with the Rival Pro (and three siblings: the Sensei Pro, and a Mini equivalent of each).

This is a latest wireless asymmetrical mouse with one key sales pitch: instead of using a wired, Bluetooth or 2.4GHz connection, it uses Ultra-wideband (UWB), a short-distance high-power connectivity which avoids interference from all your other gadgets (by virtue of the fact that none of your other gadgets are using it). It works well – and it’s not the only smart decision SteelSeries has made in the mouse.

Sources indicate that the Rival Pro sells for $179.99 / £169.99, so it’s a premium option matching the likes of the Razer Deathadder V4 Pro. If UWB isn’t a massive draw, you’ll find that price pretty intimidating, but the connectivity wasn’t the best part of the mouse to me: the “unlimited” battery system was.

To cater for UWB’s power draw and its short range, SteelSeries includes a base station which connects to your PC and is placed on the desk. Like many of the best gaming mice, this acts as a signal receiver but also a battery charging dock, so you’ve always got one cell powering up while you game.

In a recent development, you’ll pay that same price for the Rival Pro Mini, Sensei Pro, and Sensei Pro Mini. What’s the difference with those siblings? Sensei is a symmetrical alternative to the asymmetrical Rival, and both Mini equivalents are for smaller hands. Under the hood, there’s no difference in how any members of the family operate.

Industry observers note that steelSeries has kept the look of the Rival Pro pretty understated – at least, compared to the likes of its lurid Aerox 3. It comes in white or black, with the orange scroll wheel and gray brand logos the only exceptions from that uniformity. The Rival, unlike Sensei, is an asymmetrical model, but it only has a slight cant – don’t expect anything dramatic like the Logitech G502 X Plus or Razer Naga V3 Pro.

In a recent development, the standard Rival model measures 120.7mm long and 65.4mm wide, and it’s not the biggest mouse out there, but you’d need especially large mitts to find it too small. The DPI and power button is on the bottom, next to the removable battery which you retrieve with a small twist.

According to recent reports, you get two batteries: one for the mouse, and the other powering up in the base station, to counter how power-hungry UWB can be. Switching them around is quite easy – if you’re in the heat of a game, it’ll take you roughly five seconds to remove the mouse cell, retrieve the battery in the base, and insert it into the mouth. Frankly, I loved how convenient the process was: no more remembering to plug your mouse in when you’re not using it.

The Rival is made of a plastic that felt a little cheap and flimsy in my hand, more so than other gaming mice I’ve tested, and the 49g weight (which is lighter than many rivals) didn’t do much to reduce the notion that this mouse could be frail. For what it’s worth, this didn’t affect gameplay much, but it makes me worry whether it’ll last for the years of gaming that you’d expect.

A key part of the Rival Pro is the base station, which comes included in the box. It plugs into your PC via a USB-C port, and has to be positioned on your desk near your mousemat – UWB isn’t a long-distance connection medium.

The cable is two meters, which was long enough to get the hub to a good position on my desk despite my rig not being under stated desk, though people with smaller or cluttered tabletops may find positioning it an unwelcome extra task. The station doubles as a charging dock for a spare battery, so you’ve always got a charged cell on hand for when you need to swap them around.

The SteelSeries GG app isn’t necessary for using the Rival Pro – I only downloaded it two weeks into testing – but it’s where the meat lies. Here you can set up different performance profiles for the mouse (pressing the base station button toggles them on the fly), each with customized polling rate and sensor report rate. You can even overpoll up to 9kHz using it.

There are a few other features like the ability to adapt the mouse’s directions to your natural hand rotation, change movement speed acceleration or deceleration, reassign the mouse buttons and more – most of the customization you’d want, in other words. Some features are available on SteelSeries’ browser-based app equivalent, if you game on the go, but the juciest ones require the install.

Sources indicate that steelSeries’ claims that the Rival Pro has an “unlimited battery life” are a little tongue-in-cheek – it’s not wired, after all –, but the aforementioned battery-switching solution does remove charging the mouse from the equation. I’ll happily call this power system the best part of the mouse.

Industry observers note that the exact battery life per charge depends on your polling rate – at 1K you’ll be able to game for about 60 hours, but that drops to around 16 hours at the heights of 8K. A note: by default there’s no way to know the mouse charge, and a few times my mouse disconnected at unfortunate moments because I didn’t know it was low. However in the SteelSeries GG app, you can change the base station LED to indicate mouse battery, which was invaluable.

One of the core selling points of the SteelSeries Rival Pro is its use of Ultra-wideband (UWB) connectivity; this short-range, high-power standard has been used sparingly in the tech world so far, mostly used for tracking tags and certain device hand-off features (and a tiny number of desktop gadgets including, as it happens, a pair of headphones I was testing at the same time).

It has been revealed that UWB hits 6GHz, but a gaming mouse doesn’t need the kind of power it offers – though the ability to over-poll doesn’t hurt. Instead, the whole point is to avoid interference from other gadgets. Homes are full of gadgets which put out 2.4GHz and 5GHz frequency streams, especially if your desk already has some wireless gaming gadgets, which runs the risk of interference and a choppy connection. UWB avoids all that – it’s like taking a scenic flyover over traffic-ridden streets.

Now the caveat: not everyone will find UWB brings a marked improvement in their mouse responsiveness. If you only have a few wireless gadgets, or prefer to play games which don’t need lightning-fast and accurate clicks, the Rival Pro isn’t going to change much. I wasn’t somehow better at Nioh 3 or Total War by using the mouse. SteelSeries is pitching it as a ‘Pro Gaming Mouse’ and it’ll best be enjoyed by people who do find interference a problem, or playing primarily fast-paced online games.

Recent findings suggest that despite the novel feature set being a primary selling point, SteelSeries hasn't slouched on the technical side. The Rival Pro hits a 42,000 DPI count, 800 IPS and 8K polling (and that's at its highest 'standard' setting, but with over-polling you can go up to 9K). It's a fast, responsive mouse, that'll treat you well in fast action titles.

Best of all, the SteelSeries GG app gives you scope to customize the sensitivity and performance, so you can jump between different combinations of the specs depending on the game you're playing.

The main mouse buttons feel smooth to click, wherever you press on the face, and the two side buttons have a hearty heft to them (even if their height meant I had to get used to their position, compared to some alternatives I've used recently, and are a little harder to hit quickly in the heat of the moment). I can see some accusing them of being a touch too hard to press, and it takes some momentum, but I appreciate the fact it removes the prospect of accidental clicks.

It's certainly not the quietest mouse in the world, with the exception of the mouse wheel, which is smooth to use and easy to press in without much effort. It's not the most precise wheel in the world, as its rungs feel a little easy to jump between accidentally, but in practice this never had a demonstrable effect on my performance.

It has been revealed that A DPI button on the bottom of the mouse lets you toggle between various customizable profiles, of different polling and sensor report rates. This doesn't mean you can't adjust it during gameplay, though, as a button on the base station has the same effect.

In terms of specs and design, the SteelSeries Rival Pro doesn't quite match a few of its same-priced rivals. Some of the best gaming mice have robust switches, fine-tuned bodies and DPI and IPS counts which blow past this model, and if you need a pure performance model, it might not be the best option.

However it's not trying to be the best mouse, but an alternative to the top picks which relies heavily on its unique features. And if you find interference gives you a big problem when gaming, or you keep forgetting to charge your mouse, then the UWB and battery solution could be genuine gamechangers. As stated already, I found the battery feature fantastic, and I know moving over to another mouse is going to be a chore.

Recent findings suggest that I connected the SteelSeries Rival Pro to my custom-built PC, and used it daily for just under four weeks. This included using it for work, but of course also for gaming. I tested it on contemporary titles like Nioh 3 and Ark Raiders to make the most of its performance, but also spent countless hours simply playing the games I'm personally working through too, so titles like Terrascape, Rogue Waters, Total War: Pharoah and Old School Runescape gave me ages with which to get comfortable with the mouse. For more information on how we test gaming mice, check out the full GamesRadar+ Hardware Policy.

We're also rounding up the best wireless gaming mouse models and the best gaming keyboards for more options.

10 Best Warhammer 40k Survivors in Warhammer Survivors
