Latest Update: 10 Great Games That Defined The Xbox Series X|S

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1496 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s rare for gaming brands to last through three console generations, let alone four.
  • However, Xbox’s fourth and current console generation, the Xbox Series X|S, has been impacted by an ongoing identity crisis for the brand, with Xbox initially focusing on acquiring studios, Game Pass, and Play Anywhere, only to lay off hundreds of employees and refocus on developing exclusive titles.
  • Despite that rocky history, there were still many great exclusive and Microsoft-supported games that launched on the Xbox Series X|S and showcased Xbox’s ever-changing priorities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s rare for gaming brands to last through three console generations, let alone four. Microsoft’s gaming brand, Xbox, has managed to do just that, reaching the momentous milestone of creating gaming memories for 25 years.

However, Xbox’s fourth and current console generation, the Xbox Series X|S, has been impacted by an ongoing identity crisis for the brand, with Xbox initially focusing on acquiring studios, Game Pass, and Play Anywhere, only to lay off hundreds of employees and refocus on developing exclusive titles.

Despite that rocky history, there were still many great exclusive and Microsoft-supported games that launched on the Xbox Series X|S and showcased Xbox’s ever-changing priorities.

In 2014, Microsoft acquired Mojang and the greater Minecraft franchise. Since then, Microsoft has been striving to expand the Minecraft franchise through spinoffs like Minecraft: Story Mode, Minecraft Dungeons, and, for the Series consoles, Minecraft Legends.

Developed by Mojang and Blackbird Interactive, Minecraft Legends is a cross between traditional action games and RTS titles, having players acquire resources and mobs like Golems to defend the world against invading Nether forces.

Like many Minecraft spinoffs, Legends’ reception was overall mixed between critics and gamers, but its unique gameplay style goes to show just how much endless potential the Minecraft franchise has beyond its humble survival origins.

The British video game developer Ninja Theory soared into gaming prominence with the release of the ambitious action-adventure game Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice, but that game’s success wound up being a blessing and a curse: NT was acquired by Microsoft shortly thereafter in 2018.

Since then, Microsoft helped fund and publish the MOBA Bleeding Edge as well as Hellblade’s sequel, Senua's Saga: Hellblade II, which followed series protagonist Senua once again as she sets out to free her people from captivity in Iceland during the ninth century.

While Hellblade II would receive critical praise for its story and gameplay just like its predecessor, its success was apparently not enough for Microsoft to continue investing in NT, with the developer now facing closure and a third Hellblade game facing cancellation.

Recent findings suggest that double Fine is well-known for creating some of the most creative and hilarious games of the 21st century. They also have a long history with Xbox, having released Psychonauts as a timed original Xbox exclusive and Iron Brigade as an Xbox 360 exclusive.

However, Double Fine briefly joined Xbox Game Studios in 2019 to release Psychonauts 2 and its first Series X|S exclusive, Keeper, a very unique adventure game following a living lighthouse as it sets out to help a bird called Twig reunite with its flock.

Despite its rather bizarre, Dr. Seuss-like nature, Keeper wound up being a very fun, visually wondrous, and heartwarming game that every Double Fine fan and Series X|S owner should give a try, even if Double Fine is no longer a part of Xbox Game Studios.

Bethesda and Microsoft have often worked together to release some of the best RPGs as timed exclusives on Xbox consoles, such as The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind, but their relationship solidified in 2020 when Microsoft officially acquired ZeniMax Media and its studios including Bethesda.

Recent findings suggest that this led Microsoft to make Bethesda’s first brand-newly introduced RPG in years, Starfield, a timed Series X|S exclusive. The game takes place in the early 24th century in Alpha Centauri human colony worlds and sees players join Constellation, the last group of space explorers.

While Starfield turned out to be not as impressive as similar space-based games like No Man’s Sky and The Outer Worlds, it still managed to deliver engaging FPS combat and third-person spaceship piloting, as well as a wide variety of customization options for the Spacefarer, ship, and bases.

In 2023, Microsoft made the record-breaking acquisition of Activision Blizzard for $75.4 billion. Since then, most Activision Blizzard games have been optimized and intended for Series X|S play, with one of Activision's best games released under Microsoft ownership being Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

The fourth and final entry in the 2019 Call of Duty: Modern Warfare reboot series, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 features a campaign split between Captain John Price hunting down Vladimir Makarov and South Korean soldiers fighting a North Korean invasion.

MW4 is easily the best Call of Duty campaign released in years, ending the new MW series in an arguably far better way than the original MW3 and hopefully setting the stage for more great COD campaigns to come in the near future.

Obsidian Entertainment is famous for creating some of the best RPGs ever made, such as Fallout: Newly introduced Vegas and South Park: The Stick of Truth, but recently they’ve increasingly become known for creating some of the most fun survival multiplayer games, such as Grounded 2.

Set two years after Grounded, Grounded 2 sees the same kids from the first game once again shrink down to the size of insects as they struggle to survive in the public Brookhollow Park, where grass now appears like a vast jungle and spiders are monolithic predators.

Grounded 2 is still in early access, but that doesn’t stop it from being one of the most fun multiplayer games to play on Series X|S consoles, with players being able to explore and craft in over eight distinct biomes on foot or by tamed bug mounts.

As a part of ZeniMax’s acquisition, Microsoft also acquired the Sweden-based MachineGames, famous for developing the newly introduced Wolfenstein series of games. In 2024, it released one of the most surprising hits of the current console generation, with Indiana Jones and the Great Circle.

Released as a timed Series X|S exclusive, Indiana Jones and the Great Circle is a primarily first-person adventure game, following the famed archaeologist in between the first and third movies. He sets out to discover the secret behind the global Great Circle before his enemies do.

While Indiana Jones and the Great Circle doesn’t have Harrison Ford reprise his iconic role, it’s easily the best Indiana Jones story to appear since 1989 and is a pure fun, pulp adventure that any fan of Steven Spielberg and George Lucas’ movies will enjoy.

The Xbox One era was a rough time to be a Halo fan, and sadly, the Series X|S era wasn’t much different. Halo Studios, formerly 343 Industries, only released one brand-fresh Halo game on the platform: Halo Infinite.

In a recent development, the sixth mainline entry in the Halo series, Halo Infinite sees Master Chief attempt to defeat the now tyrannical Cortana on Zeta Halo, only for the Banished from Halo Wars 2 to ambush the UNSC. Master Chief, a Pelican pilot, and a new AI called The Weapon must attempt to defeat the Banished alone.

In a recent development, infinite may have launched without Forge, campaign co-op, and a lack of several multiplayer modes, but it still wound up featuring a fun multiplayer that aimed to return the series to its more classic roots. An emotional campaign story set in the series' first true open-world setting on Zeta Halo, it's not to be missed.

Recent findings suggest that for 44 years, Microsoft has stood as an innovative pioneer in the realm of flight simulation games, through its long-running Microsoft Flight Simulator series. In 2024, Asobo Studio and Microsoft released the most realistic and visually impressive entry yet, with Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024.

A direct follow-up to 2020’s Microsoft Flight Simulator reboot, Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 features much of the same core gameplay as its predecessor, but with a ton of new additions such as an in-depth career mode, dynamic environmental events and wildlife, and a plethora of new aircraft to fly such as airships and gliders.

Industry observers note that microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is easily one of the most relaxing and awe-inspiring games to play in the Series X|S era, as people can fly practically any aircraft they want in first or third-person all over the globe. Iconic locations including Zion National Park, Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park, Rio de Janeiro, and more are available as awe-inspiring sights.

Without a doubt, the best game that truly defines the Xbox Series X|S era and showcases the power of the console, as well as the potential future of the Xbox brand, is The Coalition's Gears of War: E-Day.

The sixth mainline entry in the Gears of War series and prequel to the first Gears game, Gears of War: E-Day has players once again embody the iconic duo of COG soldiers Marcus Fenix and Dominic Santiago, as they witness the Locust’s first attack on humanity in the city of Kalona on Emergence Day.

Industry observers note that returning to the franchise’s gritty, more horrifying roots, E-Day is to many Xbox fans the best Gears game since Gears of War 3, as it not only features an epic yet somber campaign but features a highly addictive multiplayer spearheaded by the newly introduced PvE mode Horde Siege. Every element of the series at its best.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that you can check out this upcoming version of the trailer below, perhaps pop it on while you have a read of the rest of this post, as Hulick did also write in a Patreon blog about his experience with the series.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that by this point I'm probably safe in assuming that you all know EA are shutting down BioWare, and that Mass Effect 5 has been cancelled in turn. You may have also seen that an internal trailer for Mass Effect 5, or Universe as it was seemingly going to be called, was leaked not long after the news broke, and that Sam Hulick, one of the composers on the original trilogy of games, shared he was going to offer up his re-scored version of the trailer. Well, it's N7 Day, as rough as that will be for many of the developers on the game, but Hulick has stood by his word, and shared an oral glimpse at what the world of Mass Effect Universe could have sounded like.

Recent findings suggest that you can check out this upcoming version of the trailer below, perhaps pop it on while you have a read of the rest of this post, as Hulick did also write in a Patreon blog about his experience with the series. "As part of my own closure, and as a love letter to the fans, I really wanted to re-score the leaked Mass Effect Universe trailer in time for N7 Day this year," he wrote. "BioWare edited a killer track called “Quartz” by French 79 to fit their trailer, which I think hinted at a slight directional shift in the score. Using that as inspiration, along with the musical tone from my work on the first three Mass Effect games, I hit the studio and got to work.".

In a recent development, as it turns out, BioWare had actually reached out to Hulick asking him to potentially do some work for the project. "This year, BioWare emailed me asking if I was interested in working with them on an internal demo, and they stated they were 'hoping to get some music written that would feel like Mass [Effect], supporting our newly introduced direction.' Of course, I said yes!" This doesn't mean he wouldn't have composed the actual game, as a composer hadn't been officially selected, but Hulick said he was "more than happy to collaborate on the new game’s musical direction and help make their internal demo sound as good as it could.".

Hulick also spoke of some of the ideas he had for the direction Mass Effect Universe's soundtrack could take, noting how he "thought it would’ve been incredible to bring more songs with lyrics into the game," considering how many people loved the first game's end-credits song. "This would’ve been a great way to highlight more emotional moments in the narrative. Artists at the top of my collaboration list included Gunship, NINA, and The Midnight, all of whom have a moody, cinematic synthwave vibe that would’ve meshed well with the score in my head. And I’m pretty sure the Gunship guys are gamers, and if they’re Mass Effect fans, that would’ve been the icing on the cake!".

It has been revealed that of course, with the studio now closing, this never got to go very far, the news hitting Hulick "particularly hard, as the Mass Effect trilogy is a core part of my origin story as a composer." For the composer, ultimately "this trailer is my way of saying goodbye… at least for now." This continues to be a horrendously sad moment in the industry! As always, solidarity with the team at BioWare.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another upcoming entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

Sources indicate that the Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That remarked, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

It has been revealed that speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

In a recent development, the game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article was produced in collaboration with our sponsor, G2A.COM.

Sources indicate that as console prices continue to rise, more people are turning to PCs for their gaming needs than ever before. The trouble is, PCs, and the components you need to make them run well, are getting pretty pricey too. It’s more vital than ever to try and make your PC do everything you want it to do for less, and that means focusing on the software rather than the hardware.

Whether you have a top-of-the-range PC that could be performing even better, or a PC with lower specs that you want to get more out of, having the best programs and software installed is key. Below you’ll find five essential pieces of software that should be installed on every gaming PC, all of which are presently available at G2A.COM for less.

Windows is the operating system that everyone thinks of first when they hear the term OS. The thing is, not all versions of Windows were created equal. Windows 11 is great, particularly for gaming, but if you really want to harness all of your PC’s power and all of its RAM, you really should be using Windows 11 Pro.

Sources indicate that VPNs are becoming more and more commonly used by just about everyone. If you have a gaming PC but you don’t have a VPN, you’re doing yourself a disservice. You should have one for a multitude of reasons, and if you’re going to get one, then you may as well make it the industry standard, NordVPN.

Recent findings suggest that VPNs can protect gamers from DDoS attacks, whether they be the kind that target entire games and studios, which are unfortunately becoming more common, or the kind that focus on you, courtesy of a disgruntled rival you may have bested in an online lobby overreacting to their defeat. A VPN also means you can bypass regional restrictions and grab games that might not be available in your part of the world.

As for why NordVPN, the gold standard offers military-grade encryption that offers better security and protection than just about any rival VPN on the market. It also offers two additional security protocols so that even the actions between your PC and the VPN itself can be masked.

As touched upon when discussing NordVPN, security on your gaming PC is of the utmost importance. Particularly in the present day when pretty much all games require you to be online - even most of the “offline” single-player ones.

You’d be surprised how many people simply leave their PC security up to the programs that come pre-installed. They’ll protect you to an extent, but if you want to fortify your virtual walls and really make sure nothing sneaks through, you should invest in Bitdefender Total Security.

Recent findings suggest that bitdefender is always running in the background, keeping your PC safe from any threats while not compromising your system’s performance. It is second to none when it comes to detecting malware, and best of all for this topic in particular, it has a dedicated Game Mode. Turn that on, and Bitdefender will never interrupt you while you’re playing.

Sources indicate that have you ever been playing a game on your PC that should look and run a lot better than it does? Or been sitting with a new game in your virtual cart, wondering if your setup will be able to run it at its best? Well, there’s software for that. A program that will test everything about your PC and its capabilities that checks back in with you to let you know what it can handle, or why it can’t handle what you expect from it.

That program is called 3DMark. 3DMark can check in on all sorts of internal details and potential problems with your PC that let you know where you might need to upgrade, or what needs to be fixed. It will automatically let you know what your PC’s ideal benchmark is, estimate how games will perform based on those results, and monitor important variables such as CPU temperature, speed, and framerate.

Industry observers note that for millions of you, playing games online with others doesn’t just mean online multiplayer. It means streaming your gameplay for the world to see, potentially to massive audiences, and most of the time while you talk over your gameplay and engage with your audience.

A documentary detailing the history of beloved Mass Effect studio BioWare is releasing next year, and will cover last month's shock closure of the studio, following the private acquisition of owner EA.

Mass Effect: The BioWare Story (per Deadline) has been written and directed by Akash Sherman and produced for Canada's Super Channel. It documents the studio from the early days after its founding in 1995 to the release of barn-burner hits like Mass Effect and Dragon Age. Filming began two years prior to the announcement of BioWare's closure and continued throughout, with Deadline reporting the documentary will "capture BioWare’s final chapter.".

It has been revealed that the BioWare Story includes interviews with studio founders Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk, and Augustine Yip, alongside Mass Effect director Casey Hudson, other BioWare developers, and Shepard voice actor Jennifer Hale. That's alongside former EA CEO John Riccitiello, LucasFilm Games vice president Douglas Reilly, and creator of The Game Awards Geoff Keighley.

According to recent reports, "The BioWare founders are my hometown heroes,” writer and director Sherman said in a statement accompanying the documentary news. "It's a privilege and responsibility to share the journey of underdogs who came together to create deeply beloved storytelling. Their golden era kindled a spark in me and in an entire generation. With the studio's recent closure, the film is now a profound valediction.".

For fans outside Canada, Mass Effect: The BioWare Story is planned for a major film festival run and a world premiere next year. No exact release date has been established as of writing.

Members of the games industry have lambasted EA's decision to close Bioware in the weeks since the news was shared, with legendary designer Warren Spector writing, "Anyone who participated in this travesty should be ashamed". Meanwhile, a petition has reached enough signatures for the Canadian government to potentially rescue the studio from closure. Whether or not it actually does… Well, weirder things have happened?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

It has been revealed that immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game promptly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a substantial launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

I know what you want. The humble city builder isn't enough for you any more, is it? It has been revealed that county of Fortune just landed in early access a couple of days ago, and as mentioned (and as the name suggests), you're building up an entire county! "You place whole settlements across the county and lay each one out on a medieval grid. Each one grows, specializes, and knits into a living region where rivers and resources decide what thrives," the game's Steam page explains. "As the county matures, a second game begins. Named mayors run each settlement. Rival noble houses weave politics across the region. And migrating cultures bless some villages, while complicating others.".

To start with, it's up to you where you want to place each of your settlements, deciding how they individually function as you do. The towns are then partially procedurally generated as they get built up, slowly connecting to other nearby towns. "The scale is the point. You are not zooming into a single town - you are zooming out to see a whole county come to life." A significant part of the strategy comes down to how you navigate the map; finding resource deposits, picking appropriate terrain profiles, utilising rivers efficiently, finding a good climate, setting good trade routes, it's all about working with the land you've got.

It has been revealed that each settlement will produce different things depending on the materials available to them in close proximity, meaning each one has a unique function. You've got different types of characters to consider too: mayors, noble houses and cultures, all intersecting with different elements of how a town functions. Seems like a unique approach to city building! And as mentioned, it's out in early access; you can pick it up on Steam here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that yesterday, Nier: Automata received a new patch on Steam, adding more language support to the title - it can now be played with Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese options - but this new upgrade also, somehow, inflated the file size of the game on PC from about 50GB to 366GB. D'oh! What's worse is, the update is not optional.

The cause of this, reportedly, is a bug that caused all the DLC in the YoRHa Edition of the game to become the same size as the base game - and the new download stacks them all concurrently. "Only SquareEnix can turn 40GB into 366GB with 8GB patch," notes one dissatisfied Steam reviewer.

If you don't have space for this massive new file on your PC (and I can't say I blame you, it's ridiculous), there is a workaround, as confirmed by Square Enix in a tweet via its Japanese Twitter account.

"We have confirmed an issue where, following the latest enhancement to the Steam version of Nier: Automata, the installation process indicates that more storage space is required than expected," noted the publisher. "We are currently investigating the cause and working on a solution. We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience. As a temporary workaround, you can download the base game by unchecking the DLC under Steam → Properties → DLC.".

It's quite ironic, really, that so many Steam reviewers are complaining about things like "I just need to delete 90% of my computer to install this" when a large part of the game is managing the software/programmes installed on your android protagonists in order to upgrade your abilities and stats. There's even an ending for uninstalling your OS on your mechanical main characters. I'd be inclined to suggest this is some sort of meta psy-op from creator Yoko Taro, but… nah, that's just fantasy, isn't it? Isn't it?

Speaking of Taro, earlier this year we learned that "Nier Automata will continue", though we only heard back in 2025 that most of the projects the developer was working on were cancelled. One of these may have been the Tencent-backed Nier mobile game in 2024, which reportedly "struggled to find a monetisation to offset its high costs.".

  • Industry observers note that the Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era.

  • The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

Recent findings suggest that the two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Industry observers note that created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Industry observers note that alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

According to recent reports, it is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

In order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In the blog post announcing the new features, Maxis said that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

Recent findings suggest that you can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Years ago, I had this dream where I was parkouring through a greatly sunken version of Venice, no doubt sourced from the many hours I put into Assassin's Creed 2 as a teen who should have been studying for their GCSEs a lot more than they were. It's stuck with me after all this time mostly because of how much I wanted to capture that feeling again somehow, as the real Assassin's Creed didn't quite cut it. And lo and behold, there I was today browsing Bluesky when I came across Boars in Rome, a Mirror's Edge and Counter Strike Surf inspired parkour platformer set in a dystopian version of Rome.

In a recent development, truthfully, witnessing the clip I've shared below was baffling to me. "This is what I dreamt of!" More or less, anyway, for the setting isn't quite the same; "You have been selected to start a new life off planet. Earth has been abandoned," explains the game's Steam page. "Machines keep working and nature claims what remains. Find out what happened while you were frozen in time by exploring the remnants of Rome where historical monuments mix with futurist megastructures.".

It has been revealed that mirrors Edge x Counter Strike Surf where you parkour on anything! Be smooth n stylish in dystopian Rome. Or just jump around and explore, whatever works for you. It's called Boars in Rome! #PitchYaGame[image or embed].

According to recent reports, not all of it matches that dream of mine, some of it leans much more into brutalism than the typical, much older architecture you'd expect of Rome, but it's there nonetheless. In motion, Boars in Rome feels quite oneiric too. There is so much more control over the game's avatar than what my real body is capable of, or wants to do. You can run, jump, slide and wallrun, positioning it quite closely to VHOLUME mechanically. Where it differs is in its additives, movement tech like being able to swing on lampposts or vault over low down obstacles.

VHOLUME is more of a game about providing you with a simple toolkit and leaving you to push it to its maximum. Boars in Roam is a touch more expressive, and I'd dare to even call it an immersive sim. The levels you can romp around are linear, you have an end point to reach, only the journey is up to you. It certainly feels appropriate to put it in the im sim camp given that, at least the game's first level, calls to mind Viktor Antonov's work on Dishonored (and Half-Life 2, too, honestly).

Hop over to Forza Horizon 6, and you’ll find the GR GT Anniversary Livery. Another one that’s easy to claim, as it should be waiting for you in the game’s Gifts tab.

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (439 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever has received its first major hotfix patch, which among other things has put an end to an especially powerful bug that made PvP battlegrounds like Warsong Gulch favoured to the Horde's advantage.
  • While Taurens are running, they gradually build up stacks of increased movement speed.
  • The Hotfix, detailed in this Blizzard blog post, stops the Tauren's plainsrunning passive from stacking during a battleground's preparation phase.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever has received its first major hotfix patch, which among other things has put an end to an especially powerful bug that made PvP battlegrounds like Warsong Gulch favoured to the Horde's advantage.

While Taurens are running, they gradually build up stacks of increased movement speed. They gain a two percent movement speed bonus per stack, and it stacks up to 30 times. That means a Tauren can gain 60 percent increased movement speed, though it's worth noting that when they stop moving, these stacks decrease. In short, cows run fast.

The Hotfix, detailed in this Blizzard blog post, stops the Tauren's plainsrunning passive from stacking during a battleground's preparation phase. What players were doing to exploit this was running back and forth in the minutes before the Warsong Gulch battleground let both teams loose. It's a capture the flag game mode, so once the gates opened, Taurens were sprinting ahead of everyone else, allowing them to rapidly push towards the enemy base for a potential early flag capture.

In addition, the hotfix removes any plainsrunning stacks from Taurens once they pick up the enemy flag, and prevents them from gaining stacks while the flag is in their possession. The goal of the enemy team is to stop and kill the enemy flag carrier as soon as possible, so a Tauren moving far faster than any of your team made this pretty difficult.

According to recent reports, tauren's could be tanky warriors or druids too, which further added to the difficulty in killing them. With this change they're now easier to lock down, though it's worth noting a Tauren can still make use of Plainsrunning to rush into the enemy base early. They just don't have that wild speed boost from the jump.

According to recent reports, surely this was the only reason my Alliance Warsong Gulch games were all lost this morning, and not because my faction is for chumps. In other World of Warcraft: Forever news, the launch earlier this week was applauded as one of the smoothest in the series history, save for a few broken boats and zeppelins.

In a recent development, the hotfix has also decreased the respawn time of the NPC Deathstalker Erland who is needed for an escort quest. People were mulling around his spawn and wasting away while waiting for him to respawn. Also, supply vendors on the Zephras Isle have been stocked with handy tradeskill bags that you could find in other starter zones. It's the shipping I assume, it takes a while for stock to make it all the way up there.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, as his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm.
  • Industry observers note that cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.

According to recent reports, as his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:.

Industry observers note that cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

It has been revealed that cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” claims game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

According to recent reports, in addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

Mega Man: Dual Override releases in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC. To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, diablo 4’s next, long-awaited Developer Update finally airs today. This meaty livestream was first announced nearly a month ago, when Blizzard initially revealed that the game’s next class is the Warlock.

Sources indicate that the Warlock’s initial unveiling, however, was incredibly brief, showing no gameplay. It also didn't explain how the class is going to fit within the existing roster. This all changes today.

Blizzard is bringing back its Developer Update livestream programme, which is the more structured, information-dense series of developer showcases. The focus of this one, of course, is going to mainly be on the Warlock class.

The Warlock is one of two classes coming to Diablo 4 with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion. The first, the Paladin, is already available in the game for anyone who pre-orders the expansion. The Warlock will instead arrive alongside the expansion on April 28.

The Developer Revision will also include a first look at the game’s next season (Season 12), currently set for March 10. This mini season will only last until the expansion’s release, so it’s going to be interesting to see what it brings to the game.

You’ll be able to watch the showcase live at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT on Diablo 4’s official YouTube, Twitch, and Twitter channels. We’ve embedded the YouTube and Twitch players below for your convenience.

Recent findings suggest that among the topics the Developer Upgrade will cover are the Killstreaks system, as well as Bloodstained items. As always, you can also expect a Q&A segment at the end of the show, and I imagine there’s going to be a few about the Warlock.

Review: Mobapad M12 Pro Joy-Con For Switch 2 - The Best Option For Handheld

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (873 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mobapad's M12 HD Joy-Con for Switch 2 were exceptional.
  • In a recent development, yet with the absence of mouse controls, I found myself returning to the console’s default Joy-Con 2 until they once again became my go-to options.
  • The fresh M12 Pro Joy-Con eliminate almost every concern I had with their HD predecessors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mobapad's M12 HD Joy-Con for Switch 2 were exceptional. They are, in many ways, superior to Nintendo’s official offering, largely thanks to the ‘smooth-gliding’ TMR sticks, satisfying mechanical inputs, and comfortable design.

In a recent development, yet with the absence of mouse controls, I found myself returning to the console’s default Joy-Con 2 until they once again became my go-to options. To be clear, I rarely use mouse mode, but the knowledge that I couldn’t was enough to sway me.

The fresh M12 Pro Joy-Con eliminate almost every concern I had with their HD predecessors. Available for pre-order at $119.99 (down from the regular price of $149.99), they include every feature from the official Joy-Con 2 – yes, everything. So you’ve got NFC support, 9-axis gyro, mouse controls, a proper ‘C’ button, and HD rumble that feels just as good as the real deal.

Add in the TMR sticks, a proper D-pad, and remappable back buttons, and you’ve got a pair of Joy-Con that, if you can stomach the price, are unquestionably the best option for handheld play.

Since I’ve already reviewed the M12 HD, I’ll focus primarily on the latest features in the Pro.

To start, the Joy-Con use Switch 2 protocol for connection, meaning the console recognises them as official Switch 2 accessories. This allows for instant connection, no faffing around with pairing settings, and of course, wake-up support with a simple click of the Home button.

Utilising the Switch 2 protocol also ensures that NFC support is always active and not reliant on a Bluetooth toggle, while the Pro now also sports a dedicated ‘C’ button – the HD’s use of a macro to navigate to the Chat app was fine, but a proper button is much better.

Finally, the little on-screen animation when you snap the Joy-Cons in place actually matches the new colour scheme (purple and green), so that’s a lovely little touch.

Mouse mode is perhaps the biggest surprise. I wasn’t expecting any third-party Joy-Con to include this for a while, but to see Mobapad pull it off so well is awesome. Like the official Joy-Con, you can use mouse controls on multiple surfaces, including a pair of jeans, and it remains accurate with minimal lag. What’s more, the ergonomic shape of the M12 Pro means that mouse mode actually feels reasonably comfortable for a change.

Industry observers note that using the face buttons and analogue stick at the same time still feels a tad awkward, but I actually feel like I can grip the Joy-Con properly while moving it across a surface. I can’t say the same for the official Joy-Con 2.

Rumble has also been upgraded. Officially dubbed ‘HD Rumble 2.0’, you can adjust the intensity via controller shortcuts, and it feels incredible. I don’t know if it’s exactly on par with the official Pro Controller, but it’s pretty damn close. In fact, you’ve probably seen videos of the Pro Controller’s rumble matching the tone of the ocarina in Zelda: Ocarina of Time. It’s remarkable stuff, and the M12 Pro does the exact same thing.

In terms of features, those are your main upgrades over the M12 HD. The design, however, has also been slightly changed. In terms of colour, you now have a gradient going from black to purple, and it looks really nice in person. I am, however, conscious that this won’t be to everybody’s taste, so I’m hopeful that Mobapad provides some expanded options in the future.

Recent findings suggest that the darker colour scheme also ensures that, like the HD, the Pro accumulates a few marks over time from fingerprints. It’s not quite so noticeable on the upper purple sections, but you might want to give them a little wipe-down from time to time. Again, some lighter colour options will help to mitigate this.

Recent findings suggest that the last change to highlight is the light-up Mobapad logo located at the bottom of both Joy-Con. I didn’t mind this on the HD, but the logo has been shrunk down drastically on the Pro, opting instead to feature a cool pattern that shimmers with the RGB lighting. It’s a lot more attractive, and looking back on the HD’s logo reveals just how garish it really is. If you’re not keen, however, you can disable the RGB functionality entirely via the Mobapad app.

It has been revealed that mobapad’s M12 HD was already a compelling alternative to Nintendo’s official Joy-Con 2, but its lack of mouse support meant that it failed to become my default option. Now, with the M12 Pro sporting every feature from the Joy-Con 2, including mouse controls and improved HD rumble, I genuinely can’t imagine using anything else.

Sources indicate that if you’re someone who enjoys playing the Switch 2 in handheld mode but finds the official Joy-Con lacking in comfort, the M12 Pro will prove a sound investment. It doesn’t get much better than this.

The sample used in this review was provided by Mobapad.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that every year, Bloodborne fans pray for the birth of another game set in FromSoftware's Lovecraftian world.
  • Asked about the noticeable lack of Bloodborne in the decade since its blood moon shone down on us all, in an interview with The Trophy Room podcast, Layden explained that returning to any beloved game is tough.
  • Sources indicate that "Bringing back old games has a certain challenge to it," he noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that every year, Bloodborne fans pray for the birth of another game set in FromSoftware's Lovecraftian world. Every year, we're no closer to a Bloodborne 2 or even a Bloodborne Remastered. But why? PlayStation's former head honcho, Shawn Layden, blames it on the tricky situation of rights ownership.

Asked about the noticeable lack of Bloodborne in the decade since its blood moon shone down on us all, in an interview with The Trophy Room podcast, Layden explained that returning to any beloved game is tough.

Sources indicate that "Bringing back old games has a certain challenge to it," he noted. "Can you do something that is not only respectful of the original, but can you, you know, recreate the phenomenon as it were?".

Industry observers note that bloodborne's situation is slightly more complicated, though. It seems that the rights are somehow split between original publisher PlayStation, developer FromSoftware and the studio's primary stakeholder Kadokawa Corporation.

"There's a lot of involved rights associated with it, and in something like that - where Sony's in there and [FromSoftware] is in there and From's parent company is in there - I think just getting everyone to sign off on the same thing is probably the biggest challenge there," Layden said.

Having led the PlayStation brand during most of its PS4 golden years, Layden mentioned working with FromSoftware on Bloodborne and the original Demon's Souls was "fantastic.".

Despite endless calls for a comeback and very stable sales more than a decade on, Bloodborne itself is still stuck on the PS4 - though it's still playable via backward compatibility on the PS5, I should add. The closest we seemingly got to a Bloodborne comeback came from Bluepoint Games, which reportedly pitched a remake sometime before parent company PlayStation shut down the acclaimed studio, though FromSoftware supposedly didn't want the project to go ahead.

Another former PlayStation executive, Shuhei Yoshida, previously speculated that Bloodborne hasn't been remade because game director and soulslike pioneer, Hidetaka Miyazaki, would prefer to handle it himself: "Miyazaki-san really, really loved Bloodborne, what he created… So I think he is interested but he's so successful and he's so busy, so he cannot do it himself, and he doesn't want anyone else to touch it.".

Elsewhere, a Bloodborne animated feature is in the works with YouTuber JackSepticEye attached as a co-producer.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love.
  • In a recent development, as is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year.
  • The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

In a recent development, as is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be unveiled tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

This batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Industry observers note that last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

According to recent reports, what do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that while its remastered upgrade might have broken cover in late September, The Witcher 3's extra expansion isn't set to join it until next year. With 2027 still a month and a bit away, a modder's taken it upon themselves to add a few more adventures to Geralt's time in Toussaint, Blood and Wine's gorgeous French-ish duchy, before the bloke from the river heads off to Letten for Songs of the Past.

Sources indicate that so far, only the opening chapter of the mod - Annals of the Duchy - has been released. It adds in a fresh quest about Geralt, with help from either Yen or Triss if either have made the trip out to Toussaint as part of your playthrough, getting into a scrape thanks to a halfling who seems to promise Gerry the chance to juice up his vineyard's vines.

The mod's creator, Jontej, has previously put together a couple of other custom Witcher 3 quests. While they do look to have used AI voices in English versions of those mods, for Annals of the Duchy they've enlisted a cast of human actors for both Enlish and Polish versions.

According to recent reports, jontej has looks to expand this newly introduced questline going forwards, having cited specific "plans for an extra storyline involving Syanna", whom you might remember from Blood and Wine's main quest. Given that - spoilers ahead - the mod relies on you having gotten the Blood and Wine ending which sees both Anna Henrietta and Syanna survive, as well as having paid to renovate the gardens of Geralt's vineyard. They add that, when it comes to their additions, the "timeline fits quite well [with] the upcoming official Songs of the Past Expansion, which has been confirmed to take place after the events of the main game/Blood and Wine".

Recent findings suggest that as much as I've argued that, as of right now, I struggle to see how Songs of the Past will manage to outdo Blood and Wine as a satisfying end to Geralt's tale in the Witcher game trilogy, I am intrigued by the idea of a few more modded adventures showing Gerry adjusting to the semi-retired life. After all, Toussaint's got to have a few more dungeons tucked away that're worth temporarily dusting off the White Wolf's twin swords for.

To kick off Annals of the Duchy, you'll need to trigger its first quest by taking a stroll from the Corvo Bianco manor house down to its gardens between 11am and 1pm. It's worth noting that any other mod which messes with Yen, Triss or companions in general has a chance to muck things up as far as Jontej's creation goes.
